t: Pure, import-free module behind the tile capsule-id chip: it shortens the host-issued surface id for display, builds the one-line "CAPSULE=... IDENTITY=..." text for an AI in a terminal, and drives the transient "Copied" confirmation. It never builds a path, reads the environment or launches anything.

A surface id is shown or copied only if it matches /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$/ (1 to 128 prompt- and shell-safe characters); anything else hides the chip (capsuleIdModel returns visible:false).
An identity (profile) name is admitted into a copied line only if it matches /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/; a missing or non-grammar identity becomes the literal "<none>" instead of being guessed.
Ids up to CAPSULE_ID_SHORT_MAX = 14 characters render whole; longer ids render as the leading 8 characters, an ellipsis and the last 5. The full id stays in the hover title "Capsule ID: <id>".
The ready line format is "CAPSULE=<surfaceId>  IDENTITY=<profile or <none>>" (two spaces between fields); buildCapsuleReadyLine returns null when the surface id fails the grammar.

Despite its name, copyCapsuleReadyLine copies only the bare surface id, not the ready line. It refuses with reason ERR_CAPSULE_ID_INVALID for a non-grammar id and ERR_CAPSULE_LINE_TOO_LARGE above 4096 UTF-8 bytes; it never throws.

With no injected or ambient navigator.clipboard the copy returns ERR_CLIPBOARD_UNAVAILABLE; a writeText rejection returns ERR_CLIPBOARD_WRITE_REFUSED. The user sees "Copy unavailable" and the code only as the status tooltip.
On tiles in state lost or error the id stays visible but Copy is disabled with the reason "Capsule is <tile>; nothing to manage".

Copy feedback uses a generation counter: a newer click supersedes an older pending copy, whose late result is dropped. After copied/unavailable a timer of CAPSULE_COPY_CONFIRM_MS = 2000 ms returns the control to ready; dispose() stops it.

Older copy of the Dockview content router that classifies panel params as kind "graphical" (capsuleId) or "microvm" (sessionId). On this commit no ui/src file imports it; WallWorkspace.vue imports workloadPanelParams.js instead, and only tests such as ui/test/capsule-panel-routing.test.js load this file.
Unlike its successor, this router has no separate missing-id alert: every unroutable params shape renders the status line "This capsule presentation is no longer available."

Live Dockview content router used by WallWorkspace.vue for the "CapsulePanel" component: params with capsuleId go to the graphical SurfacePanel router, params with sessionId go to the consumer workload slot (the ARM64 MicroVM guest console). It does no IPC and never guesses a surface.
Panel params may carry only capsuleId, sessionId, viewMode and slotFolded; viewMode must be null or a string and slotFolded a boolean, otherwise classification returns null.

Exactly one of capsuleId or sessionId must be present. A capsuleId must be 1 to 256 characters with no whitespace or control characters; a sessionId must be 1 to 256 characters with no control characters.
Accessor or inherited params are never evaluated: a getter-backed "params" property, a non-plain prototype or any symbol/accessor key makes the panel unroutable.
A panel whose params fail classification renders the alert "Missing capsule id or invalid capsule presentation." instead of a tile.

A workload panel renders only when exactly one validated workload row has that id and a workload slot exists; otherwise the tile shows "This capsule presentation is no longer available." (for example after the guest session ends).

Turns a guest-command snapshot into one presentation tile with id "guest-console:<owner_id>:<workload_id>" and title "ARM64 MicroVM". It is a presentation identity only, never a surface id or frame authority; App.vue computes guestWorkloadTiles from it.

validGuestWorkloadTile accepts a tile only with exactly the keys generation, id, kind, snapshot, title, workload_id and recomputes the tile from its snapshot; id, workload_id and generation must match the recomputation.

Builds the default wall layout profile and migrates a stored layout through the kit decoder. ui/src/main.js uses createWallLayout for the initial/fixture layout and migrateWallLayout when reading stored bytes.
The layout scope is product "metaviewer", profileId "default", workspaceId "main-wall"; the same scope is checked again by the Electron layout bridge.
Default capsule surface is 1280 x 900 (explicitly not a fixed 16:9) and each tile reserves a 23 px footer strip.
Surface size is read in order Width, width, frameWidth, geometry.Width, geometry.width, geometry.w (same for height); a non-positive or non-finite value on either axis falls back to both defaults.
Tile grid columns: 1 or 2 tiles stay in one row, 3 to 4 tiles use 2 columns, 5 or more use 3 columns; tile content keeps the surface aspect ratio inside each cell.
createWallLayout throws Error("Invalid capsule identity") for an empty or whitespace-bearing surface id and Error("Duplicate capsule identity") when two surfaces map to the same panel-<id>.
The built profile is re-decoded by the kit; a refusal is rethrown with the kit reason string, so an invalid default never reaches the wall.
Every capsule panel is id "panel-<surfaceId>", component "CapsulePanel", renderer "always", params {capsuleId}; this is the id grammar the wall controller and desktop layer rely on.

migrateWallLayout returns corrupt JSON, future schemas and wrong scopes unchanged so the kit can quarantine them; a layout holding any non-CapsulePanel or mismatched panel id is replaced with a fresh empty wall.

Measures how long a MicroVM rewind restore took, for display only (the app showed 387.5 ms on an ARM64 MicroVM [MEASURED]). Used by ui/src/components/GuestCommandPanel.vue, which calls begin() on Back and observe() on each prop update.
begin() starts timing only when the clicked action equals, key for key, the action rewindHeaderRestoreAction would build from the current props; any mismatch or a bad clock returns false.
A restore that has not reached ready within 60000 ms, a clock going backwards, or an owner/workload change clears the measurement; the user then sees no duration rather than a wrong one.

Only a successor state counts: generation and authority_epoch must both advance by exactly 1, a "restoring" phase must be observed (busy, with a pending_request_id) before "ready", and last_good_usable must equal the restored point.
The duration is rounded to 0.1 ms and kept as "confirmed" so later observe() calls keep returning it while the same generation stays ready.

Pure projection that decides whether the MicroVM tile header offers Back (rewind restore) and which restore points to list; it holds no captured authority and is re-run on current props. Imported by GuestCommandPanel.vue and restoreDuration.js.

Back is offered only when both rewind and guest sessions are held by the same owner for the same workload, neither is busy, the guest is ready with no stop/cancel control pending, the rewind phase is ready, paused or recoverable, and no request is pending.
A guest job that is still running hides Back; only a job in state exited, cancelled, timed_out or output_limit (or no job) allows it.
Only points with status "usable" are listed; in the recoverable phase the list narrows to the single last_good_usable point.
The restore action is {op:"restore", workload_id, generation, authority_epoch, point_id} and must pass rewindAction from ui/electron/rewindValues.js; otherwise null and nothing is emitted.
Any exception while projecting hides the Back control entirely (available:false, no points) rather than showing a partial menu.

Pure helpers for the per-tile capture rail: tile-scoped DOM ids and anchors, accessible names, MM:SS elapsed formatting, defensive reads of the capture store and refusal copy. A missing store disables the chrome; it never throws.
Record phases are idle, starting, recording, stopping, sealed, error and must stay identical to MV_RECORDING_PHASES; unknown phases normalize to idle.

A host refusal in entry.lastCode renders as an alert: SURFACE_UNKNOWN -> "Capture refused: this surface is not available. Reopen a live capsule."; CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE -> "Capture unavailable. Check that the capsule is live, then try again."; any other code -> generic "Capture refused..." text. Raw codes are never shown.
Record and Screenshot are disabled with "Recording is unavailable" when there is no capture store, the store says available:false, or toggleRecord/screenshot are not both functions.

Anchor segments keep canonical kebab ids as-is and encode anything else as "encoded-<4-hex per UTF-16 unit>-end"; an id already starting with "encoded-" is encoded too, so encoded values cannot collide with host ids.
Anchor family per tile: tile-<seg>-record-ai, tile-<seg>-screenshot, tile-<seg>-recording-badge, tile-<seg>-capsule-id and tile-<seg>-copy-id; DOM id and semantic anchor are the same string.
An unreadable elapsed time renders "--:--", never a fabricated 00:00.

readSurfaceEntry does a direct property get before the own-property check so a Vue reactive store tracks the key; the earlier hasOwnProperty-only read left the badge frozen on its mount-time value. Inherited keys such as __proto__ still refuse.
tileCapture.js re-exports the capsuleId.js helpers so TileCaptureChrome.vue has a single pure-module import.
Defines the seven display states of a capsule tile: connecting, live, folded (keeps capturing), human-control, agent-acting, lost and error; SurfacePanel.vue derives every tile from this module.

deriveTileState precedence: typed refusal or error transport, then unavailable transport, then departed row (lost), then terminal lifecycle (lost), then unknown lifecycle or missing row (connecting / Waiting), then stale (Stale), then non-live transport (Waiting), then attaching (Connecting), then the fold/control axis (Live).

An error tile carries status "Refused: <code>" for parity with the panel status, but the UI must render TILE_ERROR_DISPLAY_STATUS = "Surface update unavailable" and read the code via refusalCodeFor; the raw code is exposed only as the data-error-code attribute.
When the projection transport is unavailable every tile shows connecting with status "Waiting" and keepsCapturing false.
A row that disappears from a resident live or stale feed after having been seen turns the tile lost with status "Lost"; a row that never arrived stays connecting / Waiting.
Backend lifecycle destroyed maps to tile lost with status "Destroyed"; lifecycle lost maps to "Lost". Only active, standby and ceded keep capture running.
On a live row, folded wins over control; then controlOwner (falling back to the older control field) gives human-control or agent-acting; a busy AI session on shared control also reads agent-acting.

The agent chip claims motion only with evidence: aiSessionActivity "busy" or dispatchOutcome admitting, accepted or executing. Ownership alone reads "Agent ready" (the older ownership fallback made every idle agent tile read "Agent acting").
A control request without an explicit verb always resolves to take_control; release_control requires an explicit "release_control" or "surface_request.release_control" verb, even on agent rows.

presentedFrameHandle returns "" when the tile scheduler affirmatively presented nothing (unknown surface, stale generation or epoch, destroyed or contextLost), and null when presentation is unknowable; "" hides the Frame badge, null keeps it.
The freshness badge reads "Frame <generation>" from the authority-issued frame generation (a safe integer of at least 1), never a rendered-frame count.

One wall tile: wraps the kit CapsulePanel with the capture rail, network panel, paired-terminal drawer and state-controls slot, derives the tile state from the projection feed, and turns fold, pin, control, close and dock-back gestures into intents. Rendered by WallSurfaceRouter in WallWorkspace.vue.

The panel throws "SurfacePanel: invalid capsuleId: exact id required" (code ERR_PANEL_INVALID_PROP, or ERR_PANEL_INVALID_ANCHOR from anchor building) for an empty, padded, whitespace-bearing or all-digit id.

validatePanelDeps runs during setup and throws ERR_PANEL_INVALID_PROP for a missing presentationInstance, a projectionView without getSnapshot/subscribe, intentBuilders without visibility/control/presentation, or non-object registry/scheduler; tileScheduler may be explicit null.
Core refusal codes the panel knows: STALE_FRAME, SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED, LOCKED_BY_OTHER, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, OUT_OF_BOUNDS, POLICY; they are rendered distinctly, never collapsed.
Popout is always unavailable with reason "Popout is unavailable: this window denies new windows."; the other panel actions (fold, pin, control, close, dock-back, network) report available.
A tile binds only to the row whose id and surfaceId both equal its capsuleId; no fuzzy or indexed match.
derivePanelStatus is deprecated and kept only for status-parity tests; new code must use deriveTileState plus refusalCodeFor from tileStates.js.
Live rows carry only visibility; the panel mirrors it into the boolean "folded" the kit reads, because otherwise the kit re-syncs unfolded on every notice and a committed fold never hides the body.

The panel provides the kit with publicProjectionView (folded-mirrored snapshots), tileScheduler, and presentationScheduler / controlRegistry only when they expose the needed functions; placeholders are passed as null rather than as fake APIs.
lastRow remembers the last admitted row for the current capsule and feed; it resets when either changes, so a lost verdict never leaks across bindings.
Settled live tiles show status "Folded", "Human control", "Agent acting" or "Agent ready" in place of "Live"; "Agent acting" needs acting evidence on the row.
An error tile hides the capture host and shows "Surface update unavailable" (the kit readiness banner, when the row carries readinessError, owns the message instead).

A pending fold shows "Folding"/"Unfolding" until visibility, control, lifecycle, refusal code, transport status or snapshot error changes by value; then the busy label clears, so a refused fold settles too.

Fold, pin and control gestures emit "submit-intent" with bodies from intentBuilders; close and dock-back emit "presentation-intent". Handlers with no authoritative row stay silent, and the kit generic submit-intent is unwired so a gesture submits once.
State-control actions emit "state-action" only for back, save or load and only when the owner-supplied stateControls marks that action available; no default controls exist for other capsule kinds.
Authoritative visibility, not the pending gesture, calls tileScheduler.foldSurface or unfoldSurface; folding never stops capture.

A lost tile keeps its frozen last frame and Frame badge only when the row itself is lost (not destroyed or departed) and the tile scheduler still holds a presented frame handle for that generation and epoch.

Per-tile capture rail: record toggle (kit SaasRecordButton), Screenshot button, recording badge, capsule-id chip with "Copy ID for AI", and the capture refusal alert. Rendered by SurfacePanel.vue and hidden when displayOnly is true.
The record toggle is disabled with reason "An automation is recording", "Recording is unavailable", or "Recording is starting/stopping" while a host transition is pending.

An injected "automation-recording" snapshot whose identity equals the tile profile and whose phase is recording or sealing turns the badge into "Recording automation" with a Stop button (shows "Sealing…" and disabled while sealing or pending).
The kit record intent is consumed locally and turned into captureState.toggleRecord(capsuleId); it never leaves the tile as an intent.

Screenshot is momentary: a local shotCapturing flag disables the button ("Screenshot capture is pending") until the screenshot promise settles either way; the label then reads "Captured" while the store holds lastShot.
The badge reads "Error" in the error phase, "Recording MM:SS" while recording, and Starting, Stopping, Sealed or Idle otherwise.
Copy ID for AI is disabled with "Capsule is lost; nothing to manage" (or error) on blocked tiles, or "Copy unavailable" when no clipboard is reachable.
Interim empty-wall screen; a one-file seam meant to be swapped for the kit EmptyWall component without touching callers. No host calls or storage.

With no visible capsules the user sees "A clear view of your work." and the hint "No capsules are visible on this desktop. Check the Humans and Agents views..."; App.vue replaces the hint when running capsules sit in the other view.
The default action is the "Add capsule" button (id empty-wall-add, anchor wall/add-capsule) emitting "add-capsule"; App.vue opens the launcher on it.

One desktop wall: a presentation-only layer over the kit DockWorkspace (Dockview). It keeps exactly one panel per capsule id, applies tile presets, floating drag and snap, resize, reveal and layout echoes; the kit owns storage, the layout bytes and the restore barrier.
Constants: up to 256 remembered identity placements, 5000 ms orphan grace before closing a restored panel with no projection row, minimum tile 240 x 200 px, initial viewport seed 1280 x 720.
Reveal placements are closed to tab, split and floating (popout stays unavailable); local presentation verbs are close, hide, show, float and dock-back, and none of them ends a backend surface.
Every reveal or presentation intent refuses ERR_INVALID_CAPSULE_ID up front for a blank id or one containing whitespace.

findRow refuses ERR_PROJECTION_UNAVAILABLE (no view or no rows), ERR_UNKNOWN_SURFACE, ERR_ROW_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, ERR_SURFACE_GONE (lost or destroyed, unless the diagnostic allowLostSurface admits lost) and ERR_UNKNOWN_LIFECYCLE.

revealSurface refuses ERR_INVALID_PLACEMENT for an unknown placement and ERR_NOT_READY ("wall is not ready: cold restore has not settled") until the kit ready event delivered the Dockview api and window presentation.
Any Dockview exception while revealing is reported as ERR_REVEAL_FAILED with the exception message; DesktopWorkspace then counts the capsule as failed.

Identity slots: when a new surface opens for a profile (identity) that had a panel before, the stale panel is closed and the new one is placed at the remembered group, index or neighbour; a saved floating cell hint wins in floating or custom layouts.

applyPresentationIntent refuses ERR_UNKNOWN_PRESENTATION for a verb outside the closed set, ERR_NOT_READY before ready, ERR_UNKNOWN_PANEL for an absent panel and ERR_PRESENTATION_FAILED on a Dockview exception.
Closing a tile (x) removes only the dock panel and emits "panel-closed" so the shell can offer the way back; the capsule keeps running.

A float layout echo needs slot_id equal to the capsule id or "cuk-ai-slot-<id>", integer x/y in 0..16383 and width/height in 1..16384, else ERR_INVALID_PLACEMENT "Placement is unavailable."; the kit currently ignores the bounds.

A move/tab echo needs a group_id matching /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,127}$/ and an index 0..255; other ops fall through to applyPresentationIntent. The caller waits for the authority echo before applying it.
setPreset refuses LAYOUT_PRESET_INVALID "Unknown tile preset." and ERR_NOT_READY "Wall is not ready."; presets are single, side-by-side, grid, grid-3x2, focus-strip and floating, null means custom.

If applying a preset throws, the preset resets to custom and LAYOUT_PRESET_FAILED "Tile layout is unavailable." is reported through layout-error; App.vue shows "Tile layout is unavailable. Try again after the desktop is ready."

Every 150 ms the wall re-runs refreshPreset: it retitles panels, closes destroyed panels, prunes orphans and re-applies the preset only when its signature (preset, size, tile ids and hidden flags) changed.
A restored panel is closed only after its surface has been absent from a live, non-stale projection for 5000 ms, so a projection that is still filling never drops a live tile.

resizeTile refuses ERR_NOT_READY before ready, LAYOUT_SIZE_INVALID "Unknown tile or size action." and LAYOUT_SIZE_FAILED "Tile size is unavailable." on exception; resizeFocused refuses ERR_NOT_READY "No focused tile.".

Each resize step is 10% of the wall dimension, clamped between 240/200 px and the wall size; any manual resize turns the desktop into a custom layout (preset null) so the 150 ms preset refresh does not undo it.
The kit ready payload must carry api.getPanel/addPanel and windows.state/show/hide/float/dock, else ERR_INVALID_READY and the wall stays not ready.

revealWorkload refuses ERR_UNKNOWN_WORKLOAD "The workload panel is unavailable.", ERR_NOT_READY "The wall is not ready." and ERR_PRESENTATION_FAILED "The workload panel could not be shown."; workload panels are "workload-panel:<id>" with minimum 320 x 240.
Floating title drags paint through a nonce-bearing style element; with no meta "*-style-nonce" the drag is silently refused (the window does not move).

Snap grid columns and rows must be integers 1..5 and the wall size positive, else floatDragBounds throws SNAP_GRID_INVALID; holding Control while dragging snaps to a grid cell, otherwise the move is free and clamped to the wall.

presetRectangles throws LAYOUT_PRESET_INVALID for an unknown preset or non-positive size and LAYOUT_PRESET_DUPLICATE for repeated tile ids; a maximized tile suspends preset layout (returns no rectangles).

focus-strip gives the leading tile 70% of the width and stacks the rest on the right; floating gives each tile 90% width, full height, cascaded 24 px; grid is 2 x 2 and grid-3x2 is 3 x 2 with extra tiles sharing the last cell as tabs.
A graphical panel whose params carry no valid capsuleId renders the alert "Missing capsule id. Reset the workspace layout."

WallMissingPanel ("Panel unavailable: <id>." / "Panel type retired. Reset the workspace layout.") is exported but not registered in panelComponents on this commit, which holds only CapsulePanel (inference: retired types are left to the kit fallback).
WallWorkspace imports the content router from workloadPanelParams.js (not capsulePanelRouter.js) and registers it as the only panel component "CapsulePanel".
Identity-slot history is trimmed to 256 entries only when Dockview exposes its panel list; active panels are never evicted.
Each wall shows Columns and Rows selects (1..5, anchors workspace/<ownerWindowId>/snap-columns and snap-rows) and the hint "Hold Control while dragging to snap"; changes emit snap-grid-change.

Multi-desktop host mounted by App.vue: it keeps the metaviewer.desktops/v1 state (Humans and Agents views, each with numbered desktops) and mounts one WallWorkspace per desktop, hiding all but the active one. Each wall gets a filtered feed and its own storage adapter.
After a failed load the desktop state is read-only and every save rejects with LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED; App.vue then records layoutUnavailable {code:"LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED"}.

Saves are coalesced: one write loop runs at a time and repeats while the dirty flag was set again; each write prunes panel references that no longer belong to the desktop. A write error emits layout-error.
Stored desktop state that fails validateDesktopState (or a legacy layout the kit decoder refuses) throws LAYOUT_CONTRACT_INVALID; the catch sets readOnly and emits layout-error.
A legacy single-wall layout is migrated by copying it into desktop 1 of both views; stale panel references are removed on save and by each wall orphan prune.
Each live row and workload tile is assigned to the view in props.modes, defaulting to "agent"; a new capsule lands on the active desktop of its view.
A fresh session with no saved layout switches to the Agents view once if every initially reported row is in agent mode; saved layouts and explicit navigation close this choice.

refreshCurrentDesktop returns ERR_NOT_READY, DESKTOP_CHANGED (desktop switched during refresh), PROJECTION_UNAVAILABLE (projection not live and fresh) or SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE with failedCapsules; it rebuilds presentation only and issues no capsule command.
Choosing the grid preset sets the desktop snap grid to 2 x 2 and grid-3x2 to 3 x 2; setPreset refuses ERR_NOT_READY before the wall is ready and LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED when read-only.

Before moving a tile to another desktop the wall asks the native globalThis.metaviewerRoles.visibility(id,false); a refusal is returned unchanged. Then the panel is closed on the source wall, the assignment moved, layouts cleaned and the state saved; target "new" returns DESKTOP_LIMIT at 16 desktops.
After a 5000 ms startup grace and 5000 ms of continuously live, fresh projection (polled every 250 ms), assignments and labels of ids not in the projection or workload tiles are deleted.

When a wall saves, each floating group position is converted to a snap cell and stored per identity in desktop.identityCells (capped at 256), so a reopened identity returns to its cell after the surface id changes.
Shortcuts arrive two ways: capture-phase keydown/keyup on the renderer window, and the "metaviewer:desktop-shortcut" CustomEvent injected by the Electron side when a native tile has focus.
forgetIdentity throws LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED when not loaded or read-only; otherwise it deletes the identity label and identity cells and saves before the identity id can be reused.
renameDesktop and renameCapsule return false while read-only, while a rename for the same key is pending, or for an invalid label; a failed save restores the previous label.
A tile the user closed stays dismissed on that desktop and is not re-revealed automatically; only a forced refresh (refreshCurrentDesktop) or an explicit reveal brings it back.
Provides "tileLayoutActions" (resize, move, transfers, focus, desktops) to descendant tile menus.

Pure model of the desktops state (schema metaviewer.desktops/v1), shared by the renderer (DesktopWorkspace.vue, App.vue) and the Electron layout bridge in ui/electron/main.js. Presentation state only.
Two views, human and agent, each with at most 16 desktops; presets single, side-by-side, grid, grid-3x2, focus-strip, floating (or null for custom).

validateDesktopState requires exact key sets at every level (no extra keys), the exact schema string, a valid activeView, desktop 1 present in each view, unique desktop ids below "next" and an active id that exists.
Optional snapGrid cols and rows are integers 1..5; optional identityCells hold at most 256 identity keys matching /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/ with col/row 0..4.

Every saved panel must belong to the desktop whose layout holds it (by assignments) and may appear only once across all desktops; assignment ids must be non-empty, whitespace-free and not __proto__/constructor/prototype.
addDesktop throws DESKTOP_LIMIT at 16 desktops in a view; the new desktop becomes active.
assignSurface throws CAPSULE_ROLE_UNPROVEN for a view other than human or agent; an existing home in the same view is kept, a view change re-homes the capsule to that view active desktop.
Desktop 1 can never be removed, nor a desktop that still has a capsule assigned; removal returns false then. After removal desktops are renumbered 1..n and assignments remapped atomically.
moveSurface moves a capsule only between desktops of its current view; role (human/agent) and backend identity are not changed here.
Older envelopes stored a leaf grid root that the kit admitted but Dockview cannot render; normalizeDesktopLayout wraps it in a branch, keeping the group and geometry.
pruneDesktopLayout drops panels whose capsule no longer belongs to the desktop, empties dead groups (kept for grid presets), and creates an empty "desktop-empty" root group when nothing is left.
Desktop and capsule display labels are trimmed, 1..80 code points, with no control or bidirectional override characters; at most 256 capsule labels, keyed by profile_id or id.

The Electron layout bridge validates every stored metaviewer.desktops/v1 payload with validateDesktopState and the kit decoder before accepting it, else LAYOUT_CONTRACT_INVALID "layout contract refused".
One chord grammar for desktop shortcuts, used both by the renderer (DesktopWorkspace.vue) and by the native tile input boundary (ui/electron/xpraHumanTile.js) so keys work whichever side has focus.
Ctrl+Alt+Arrow (no Shift or Meta) resizes the focused tile: Left narrower, Right wider, Up shorter, Down taller.
Ctrl+Tab toggles between the Humans and Agents views and Ctrl+1..9 selects desktop 1..9 (Ctrl alone, no Alt, Shift or Meta).

From a native tile the chord is forwarded by executeJavaScript as a fixed "metaviewer:desktop-shortcut" CustomEvent with a closed JSON payload (plus capsuleId for resize); delivery failures are swallowed.
A key whose keydown was captured as a chord also has its keyUp swallowed (tracked in the captured set), so the guest never sees half a chord.
xpraHumanTile.js calls interceptDesktopShortcut from the native tile webContents "before-input-event" handler.

App.vue refreshWall maps refreshCurrentDesktop codes to user text: DESKTOP_CHANGED, PROJECTION_UNAVAILABLE, SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE, ERR_NOT_READY; any other failure shows "Wall refresh did not complete. Try again."
App.vue derives at most one guest workload tile from the guest-command snapshot and passes it to DesktopWorkspace with validGuestWorkloadTile as validator.
ui/src/main.js runs every stored layout read through migrateWallLayout before the kit restores it.
GuestCommandPanel.vue owns the restore-duration measurement and the rewind header Back menu built from rewindStateControls.js.

catalogModel.js is the pure model behind the Add capsule launcher: a closed, frozen list of capsule kinds, typed error rows for unknown or malformed entries, and the builder that turns a launcher choice into a create-capsule intent. It has no DOM, framework or host calls, and its documented rule is that nothing in it throws.

The closed kind set, in display order, is identity-browser, program, host-program, desktop-window, vm (label "ARM64 Linux VM") and microvm (label "MicroVM — ARM64"). The host-program card says "Runs on your computer — not isolated."; the desktop-window card says native Wayland windows are not listed.

availableCatalogKindIds keeps every non-ARM kind and offers vm or microvm only when a host capabilities object says supported_host === true and that kind is available === true; without a capabilities object it falls back to the vmAvailable and headlessAvailable booleans, which default to false, so ARM kinds are hidden by default.

unavailableArmCapsules returns nothing on a host whose capabilities lack supported_host === true; on a supported host it lists each of vm and microvm that is not available, with the host-provided reason or the fallback "Capsule setup prerequisites are unavailable." These rows become visible but disabled launcher cards.

The model exposes three typed error codes: ERR_CATALOG_UNKNOWN_KIND (message "Unknown capsule kind: <json>."), ERR_CATALOG_INVALID_ENTRY ("Invalid catalog entry.") and ERR_CATALOG_INVALID_INTENT ("Invalid create intent.").

normalizeCatalogEntries accepts kind strings or {kind} objects, keeps the first copy of each valid kind, collapses errors by raw kind (all malformed entries share one invalid-entry row), and adds -2, -3 suffixes when error-row slugs collide; a non-array input gives empty types and errors.

buildCreateIntent returns {type:"create-capsule", kind, placement}. For program and host-program it also requires a non-empty trimmed binary and allows only role "human" or "agent"; for desktop-window it requires a window that passes normalizeWindowCandidate; any other failure yields ERR_CATALOG_INVALID_INTENT.
Placement is "tab" unless the input is exactly "split" or "floating"; anything else silently becomes tab.

normalizeWindowCandidate admits one desktop window from srf-host-window list only if xid is 1..0xffffffff (number, decimal or 0x string), the witness is 1-128 chars without whitespace or shell metacharacters, title is at most 512 chars without NUL (empty becomes "Untitled window"), program is 1-256 chars, and width and height are integers 1..4096 (default 1280x900).
normalizeWindowList is whole-list fail-closed: one invalid row, or any duplicate xid or witness, rejects the entire list with ok:false and no windows.
createInvokerFocus stores the element focused when the launcher opened and on restore focuses it only if it still has a focus function and is not disconnected; it reports whether focus moved.

CatalogLauncher.vue is the Add capsule launcher: it wraps the grouped dialog with the catalog model, lists installed and recent host apps, and runs the follow-up steps (role and identity for browsers, binary and role for programs, window choice for desktop windows) before emitting a create intent.

App.vue mounts CatalogLauncher (unless the wall is a display-only nested wall) and passes arm64-capabilities, vm-available, guest-command-available and headless-available; the launcher talks to the host through globalThis.metaviewerRoles, which rolePreload.cjs exposes over IPC channel metaviewer:roles.v0.3.

Each time the launcher opens it calls metaviewerRoles.listApps (op list-apps); it keeps at most 256 apps whose id is 24 hex chars and whose icon is empty or a PNG/SVG data URL, and at most 12 recent ids. On failure it shows "Installed apps are unavailable. Choose a capsule kind or type a binary."

dialogTypes is the card list: catalog kinds filtered by availableCatalogKindIds, then disabled ARM cards, then Recent apps, then Installed apps. Installed and recent app cards are described "Host program — not isolated". When guest commands are available the microvm card text becomes "Run commands inside an isolated ARM64 guest. No interactive terminal or desktop."

Choosing an installed or recent app opens the program step as kind host-program with the app binary filled in and role preset to human; choosing the program or host-program kind opens the same step with role human unless the payload asked for agent.

confirmProgram passes a settle callback with the create event. If no listener settles it the user sees "Program launch was not handled by the host."; a reply with ok:false shows its reason, message or code; otherwise "Program could not be started."

The browser role/identity step can show "SURFACE_CREATE_BUSY: A capsule is already starting. Wait for it to finish, then try again.", "PROFILE_ALREADY_BOUND: Check this identity in Identities and stop or reuse its existing capsule.", "NO_IDENTITY: Open Identities to add or check an available identity, then try Add capsule again." and, when the identity list fails, IDENTITY_LIST_UNAVAILABLE with its own help text.

The desktop-window step raises host_window_unavailable errors: "window listing unavailable" when the host has no listWindows, "invalid or ambiguous window list" when normalizeWindowList rejects the list, and "window listing failed" otherwise; the text is shown in the window dialog alert.

With no attachable window the list shows "No attachable X11 windows are open. Native Wayland windows are not listed."; with a search that matches nothing it shows "No open desktop windows match this filter."

A choiceGeneration counter is bumped on every open, close and new choice; async replies (choices, listWindows, program and window settles) are dropped when the generation moved or the launcher closed, so a late reply cannot reopen or fill a closed step.
forwardVisible ignores the kit dialog closing itself right after create while a role, program or window step is active, so that step is not ended; onClose likewise does nothing while a step is open.
onCreate returns at once for a disabled ARM card, so a disabled VM or MicroVM card can never produce a create intent even if the dialog emitted one.

Only browser kinds (browser, identity-browser) go through the role/identity step, and only when metaviewerRoles exists; the role defaults to agent, or to the role stored on the chosen identity unless the user edited it. Other kinds emit the intent directly.

Catalog error rows render in the dialog empty slot as "This capsule kind is unavailable." for ERR_CATALOG_UNKNOWN_KIND and "This catalog entry is unavailable." for other codes; the slot is only provided while errors or an app-list error exist, so a clean catalog keeps the kit empty text.

The host-program dialog states "Runs on your computer — not isolated. Browsers use a fresh temporary profile in RAM, never your personal profile." Stable anchors include dialog/new-capsule/program-role, program-binary, program-start and program-error.

GroupedCapsuleDialog.vue is the host copy of the kit New Capsule dialog with three grouped sections, "Capsule kinds", "Recent" and "Installed apps", while keeping the kit keyboard model, stable ids, placement modes and close behavior.

A card is disabled when its id has a disabledReasons entry; disabled cards are skipped by selection, arrow navigation and the first-selection reset, show the host reason, and show "Enable: configure verified local assets using the ARM64 capsule setup guide."
App groups (Recent, Installed apps) carry a note "Host programs — Not isolated" that each app card references through aria-describedby.

createSelected emits create with {type, placement} and then closes the dialog; Enter in the search box or the grid does the same, Escape closes, and ArrowDown from search moves to the first selectable card.

Opening the dialog resets the search, category and placement and selects the first enabled card; when a card is selected the placement resets to that card's opensAs value. Placement buttons offer Tab, Split and Floating.
Card and category anchors are dialog/new-capsule/type-<id> and dialog/new-capsule/category-<id>; the older shell/navigation/new-capsule-* anchors are kept for one release in data-anchor-alias.
The dialog wraps the vendor Dialog with createCspDialog from the kit, and caps the panel at 92dvh so the rail and grid scroll while the head, search and footer stay fixed.
catalog.css styles the launcher error rows with kit status tokens only (no color literals, no new fonts).

openingMode.js stages a one-shot opening-mode file (schema metaviewer.opening_mode/v0.3) that tells the daemon adapter whether a capsule opens under human or agent control, optionally with a host binary path or an attached host window.

stageOpeningMode throws CAPSULE_MODE_INVALID when the profile id fails ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$, the mode is not human or agent, a binary target is not an absolute path of at most 256 chars, a window target is malformed or not in agent mode, or host_xpra is set without a binary target.

A host-window target is only accepted in agent mode, with xid 1..0xffffffff, a witness up to 128 chars without whitespace, title up to 512 chars, program up to 256 chars and width/height 1..4096 (defaults 1280x900).
A foreign (protected) identity is refused with IDENTITY_PROTECTED, and the opening-modes directory must be a real directory owned by the current user with mode 0700, else CAPSULE_MODE_DIRECTORY.

The file <profile>.json is created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW and mode 0600, so a second staging for the same profile while one is pending fails instead of overwriting; a write error unlinks the file, and the function returns a cleanup that unlinks it and ignores ENOENT.

roleHost.js is the only caller: it stages agent mode with a host window for desktop-window capsules, the chosen role and binary (plus host_xpra) for program capsules, and the chosen role for identity capsules.

Mode switch path: App.vue confirmModeSwitch calls metaviewerRoles.switchMode, which rolePreload.cjs sends as op "switch" on IPC channel metaviewer:roles.v0.3; roleHost.js routes it to switchMode(surfaceId).

switchMode flips the role (human to agent or back). For a Host program (programProfiles entry with hostXpra) it stops the running surface and creates the program again with the new role, marking the profile stopping then starting: switching a Host program restarts it. Other capsules use core.switchRole and keep the running process.

switchMode refuses CAPSULE_ROLE_INVALID for attached desktop windows and VM capsules, SURFACE_CREATE_BUSY while another create runs, CAPSULE_MODE_UNAVAILABLE when the runtime has no switchRole ("The capsule is still open; use Take control / Release instead."), and CAPSULE_MODE_UNPROVEN when the switch reply or the live surface does not confirm the new role.

roleHost.js registers one ipcMain handler on metaviewer:roles.v0.3; every message must carry schema metaviewer.roles/v0.3 and an exact key set per op, else XPRA_SENDER_REFUSED or XPRA_PAYLOAD_REFUSED; list-apps returns the installed-apps inventory.

Host capability rows come from arm64CapsuleStatusSync: on a non-arm64 host supported_host is false and both vm and microvm are disabled ("ARM64 capsules are unavailable on this host."); on arm64 they stay disabled until MV_ARM64_CAPSULE_STATUS supplies a valid {vm, microvm} status.
With MV_ARM64_CAPSULES=1 main.js skips the automatic initial browser surface that a plain start creates once the adapter is live.
In MV_ARM64_CAPSULES=1 mode, a VM create is refused with VM_UNAVAILABLE unless the capability check reports vm.available.

programBinaries.js keeps one small sidecar per program profile (schema metaviewer.program_binary/v1) recording the resolved absolute binary, whether it runs as a Host program (hostXpra) and whether it is bound to an identity, outside the frozen identity contracts.

Every failure throws PROGRAM_BINARY_REFUSED: a bad profile id, a sidecar that is not a regular 0600 file owned by the user or is larger than 1024 bytes, a schema or profile mismatch, a binary that is not an absolute path up to 256 chars without control characters, or a non-boolean flag.
remember writes to a random dot-temp file opened with wx and 0600, syncs it and renames it over the target, so readers never see a half-written sidecar.

copyWith copies the sidecar to the destination profile only after the core confirms a capsule_state_event/v0.2 completed copy with the same operation id, profile and slot; the copy is marked identityBound.

hostProfiles lists Host program profiles (hostXpra and not identityBound) as rows {id, browser:"program"}; a refused sidecar is skipped so it cannot hide other valid programs. reconcile forgets sidecars whose profile disappeared from the identity list.
desktopApplications.js builds the host app inventory for the launcher from .desktop files in the user and system application folders; it never executes desktop arguments or a shell.

desktopEntry hides entries that are not Type=Application, are Hidden, NoDisplay or Terminal, whose Exec needs arguments other than file/URL placeholders, or whose binary is env, sh, bash, zsh or fish, because the Host program API accepts a binary, not argv.

Limits: at most 256 apps, 1024 .desktop files per folder, 65536 bytes per file, 12 recent ids, and 262144 bytes per icon; app ids are the first 24 hex chars of the sha256 of the file name, and a user entry with the same file name masks the system one.

Icons are read only from allowed roots and SVGs are rejected if they contain script, foreignObject, DOCTYPE/ENTITY, stylesheet imports, event attributes or any non-fragment reference; raster icons are resized to 32x32 data URLs.
launched records an app as recent only after MetaViewer's own successful Host program launch, writing recent-apps.json via a temp file and rename.

NetworkPanel.vue is the per-capsule Network dialog: it loads the capsule egress record, lets the operator choose "Open (default)" or "Dedicated proxy with allowlist", and saves it; the change applies on the next start of the capsule.
SurfacePanel.vue mounts NetworkPanel per capsule; it calls the operator host egress.get and egress.set methods with the capsule profile identity and record schema metaviewer.capsule_egress/v1.

Without an identity the panel shows "Network configuration unavailable: this capsule has no admitted profile identity."; without the egress channel "Network configuration unavailable: this build has no operator network channel."; a thrown request shows "Network configuration request failed before the adapter answered; nothing was saved."
A NET_OPEN_PREREQ refusal on save shows a "Confirm save for next start anyway" button, which resends the save with confirm:true; editing the mode or domains hides that button again.
A generation counter drops replies from older requests and closing the panel bumps it, so a late get or set cannot overwrite newer state.

refusalText maps NET_PROXIED_UNSUPPORTED, NET_OPEN_PREREQ, NET_EGRESS_IO and NET_EGRESS_INVALID to fixed operator text; any other upper-case code becomes "Network configuration unavailable (<code>)." and anything else "Network configuration unavailable."

In legacy network mode (the capsule binary declares no network modes) the panel explains the probe reason; the capsule keeps its unrestricted network and no mode is enforced. A stored allowlist record in that state warns that the next start will be refused with NET_PROXIED_UNSUPPORTED.

Allowlist entries must be 1 to 256 exact hostnames: lowercase labels with a dot and a letter, no localhost, .local, .internal, .lan or home.arpa names, no hex-looking labels. The rules mirror the preload checks, which stay authoritative.

settingsModel.js is the single closed definition of MetaViewer settings: scheme (mv-dark or mv-light), density (compact or comfortable), live wall fps (3, 30 or 60) and recording fps (1..60), with decode, encode, a store over an injected host port, a save debouncer and a wall fps meter. It never uses localStorage.
Defaults are mv-dark, compact, 30 wall fps and 3 recording fps; saves are debounced in a 150 ms window and the actual-fps readout uses a 2000 ms sliding window.

Decode codes are ERR_SETTINGS_MALFORMED, ERR_SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_KEY, ERR_SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_SCHEME, ERR_SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_DENSITY, ERR_SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_WALL_FPS and ERR_SETTINGS_UNKNOWN_RECORDING_FPS; host-level codes are ERR_SETTINGS_HOST, ERR_SETTINGS_SAVE_FAILED and ERR_SETTINGS_APPLY_FAILED.

Stored text with an unknown key, or a wallFps/recordingFps written with a fraction or exponent (30.0, 3e1), refuses as a whole so the caller uses full defaults; an invalid value of a known key only resets that field.

The float-lexeme check reads the raw number text through the JSON.parse reviver context.source and counts only top-level keys, so nested objects or string values cannot fool it; if the engine gives no source text the value refuses (strict fallback).

settingsRefusalFor turns any error into a fixed reason so host text never reaches the screen: decode failures show "Stored settings are unreadable; defaults are in use", ERR_SETTINGS_HOST "Settings host is unavailable", apply failure "Color scheme could not be applied", and save or unknown errors "Settings could not be saved on the host".
createDebouncedRunner runs the first call at once, keeps only the last value during the window and runs it when the window ends; cancel drops the queued value (used on unmount and host replacement).
The store save path encodes exactly the four keys in fixed order and treats any host acknowledgement other than true as ERR_SETTINGS_SAVE_FAILED ("Settings host refused the write").

createWallFpsMeter counts frame notices with a valid non-negative safe-integer frame_ref.ts_ns inside the window and reports arrivals per second; formatWallFpsLine shows "<requested> requested, <actual> actual" with "--" before any sample.

settingsHost.js adapts the preload settings methods to the store port; only when loadSettings or saveSettings is missing does it fall back to kit preference storage (scheme only on save), and fixture runs keep settings in memory. A host rejection never triggers the fallback.
ui/src/main.js builds the settings host with createSettingsHost and reuses createSettingsHost.decodeStoredSettings in its boot parser, so boot and the panel share one decode.

MvSettingsPanel.vue is the Settings page: hidden live session limit, color scheme, density, live wall fps with a measured readout, recording fps, and recording/screenshot folder and RAM-or-disk capture mode.

persistSettings saves first and only then applies the scheme live; if applying fails it shows ERR_SETTINGS_APPLY_FAILED, tries to restore the previous scheme and save it back, and keeps the apply refusal even if that rollback save fails.

On load, a decode failure silently falls back to defaults; a transport or host failure falls back too but shows the typed refusal row (anchor settings/save-refusal). All controls stay disabled until the load finishes and the live scheme is verified.

Recording fps input accepts only integer text, clamps it to 1..60 and reverts silently on anything else; the hidden live sessions field shows "Enter a non-negative whole number. The previous limit is still active." when the value is refused.

Capture preferences come from globalThis.metaviewerCapturePreferences; the panel says recording folder changes apply at the next app start and a host environment setting takes priority, while screenshot folder changes apply now. Without that host it shows "Recording folders are unavailable on this host."
A generation counter is bumped on each host load and on unmount; replacing settingsHost cancels the queued save and reloads, and stale completions cannot change the theme.
settings.css styles the settings panel with kit tokens only; its header says contrast pairs are checked in both schemes by the settings panel test.

handoffModel.js turns metaviewer.handoff/v1 rows (a capsule step stopped by a login wall or bot check) into plain operator notices with fixed steps; the agent never handles the check or signs in, and control and release are the operator's own actions.

Rows are keyed by surface_id:step_index and stay visible until an explicit successful acknowledge; empty snapshots, missing files or transport failures never dismiss a row, and acknowledged keys are never shown again.
load and acknowledge throw HANDOFF_UNAVAILABLE when the host list or ack reply is not ok; a failed list is never treated as an empty list.
Acknowledge sends {surface_id, step_index, gesture:"operator-acknowledge"}; the notice says Acknowledge only hides it and does not resume the run, so the operator must re-run the workflow.

HandoffNotice.vue is mounted in App.vue; it subscribes to operator host handoff updates (channel metaviewer:handoff.state in preload), emits activity code CAPTCHA_HANDOFF for each new row, emits pending surface ids, and its Take control button emits take-control, which App.vue turns into reveal plus take_control on that tile.
If subscribing or the first load fails the notice shows "Handoff notifications unavailable."; a failed acknowledge shows "Acknowledgement could not be saved. The notice stays visible."
handoff.css gives handoff rows their own refusal-tone styling and a content-sized list, separate from the activity strip.

ptySession.js is the direct-spawn seam for an Electron utility process: it validates a trusted main-supplied spawn spec (absolute file and cwd, at most 32 args, 4096-char strings, no NUL) and runs one node-pty session over a byte port with cumulative credit accounting.
Any spawn spec with extra keys, a relative file or cwd, more than 32 args, an over-long or NUL-carrying string, or a bad env name throws INVALID_SPAWN_SPEC before anything is spawned.
On the utility path, a single PTY output chunk over 65536 bytes, more than 524288 unacknowledged bytes, or 256 unacknowledged frames kills the PTY and sends OUTPUT_OVERFLOW instead of data.
An input frame whose seq is not exactly the next input sequence, or whose payload exceeds 65536 bytes, throws INVALID_INPUT; there is no retryable path here.
Output back-pressure: the PTY is paused once 131072 bytes are unacknowledged and resumed when the backlog drops under 65536 after a valid ack.
An ack must name a newer sequence and exactly the cumulative byte boundary recorded for it, otherwise INVALID_ACK is thrown.
Any port message that is not input, ack, or a resize within 1..500 cols and 1..300 rows throws INVALID_MESSAGE; CLOSED_OR_INVALID and SESSION_MISMATCH guard closed sessions and wrong session ids.
In the utility process every receive error (INVALID_INPUT, INVALID_ACK, INVALID_MESSAGE) is fatal: the PTY is killed and the port closed, without sending an error frame.
If node-pty cannot be loaded the utility posts {error:'TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE'} on the port and closes it.
One utility process binds exactly one session: the earliest parent message carrying exactly one port wins and later messages are ignored.

launchTerminalUtility forks ptyUtility.js as service 'MetaViewer PTY' and hands it the spec and port; on this commit no caller in ui/electron imports it, so the live path is the in-main broker engine (inference from grep).

terminalHost.js is the main-process terminal host: it runs the ptyBroker engine in-process over owned profiles (shell plus installed agent CLIs), hands each renderer session a MessagePort, and enforces sender binding, rate limits and pre-attach bounds.
hostBindings.js creates the single terminal host with installedAgentProfiles(env) as profiles and disposes it on app before-quit.

Per-session host limits: attach within 10000 ms, at most 64 frames or 65536 bytes queued before attach, resize 16 burst and 16/s, input 64 writes burst and 64/s and 262144 bytes burst and 262144 bytes/s.
An input frame is admitted only if it has exactly the keys bytes,seq,session, at most 65536 bytes, and seq equal to the host's last admitted input sequence plus one.

When the input rate buckets are empty the host does not admit the frame and does not advance inputSeq; it posts a retryable refusal carrying expectedSeq, and the refused bytes are not replayed by anyone.

Any input frame that fails the admission shape (wrong seq, over 65536 bytes, extra keys) is fatal: the host posts a non-retryable TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED and closes the whole PTY session. (inference) A frame already in flight after a retryable refusal carries seq expectedSeq+1 and lands here, so one rate-limit refusal during pipelined input can end the terminal; a candidate path for the open bug 'paired terminal exited after a very long typed line'.
After 64 consecutive retryable refusals (input or resize) without an admitted frame, the next refusal becomes fatal and closes the session.

Broker events become port frames: data becomes {session,seq,bytes}, exit becomes {session,exitCode} and the broker exit reason (SESSION_CAP, SESSION_EXPIRED) is dropped, so the renderer cannot tell a byte-cap or lifetime exit from a normal one.

Any broker error on an opened session (for example WRITE_TOO_LARGE, INVALID_INPUT, WRITE_FAILED, ACK_REFUSED) is collapsed to a non-retryable {error:'TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED'} frame; the broker code is lost on the port.
Output that arrives before the renderer attaches is queued; exceeding 64 frames or 65536 bytes closes the session, as does not attaching within 10000 ms.

open refuses with PAYLOAD for a bad request shape, COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED for an unowned profile or changed args, TERMINAL_DISABLED until setEnabled(true), and returns {ok:false, code:'TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE'} when node-pty cannot load.
A session is bound to the sender that opened it; a call from a different sender key throws TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED: SENDER.
In a nested display window (--nested-depth=1) every host method throws DISPLAY_ONLY: side-terminal is disabled in nested display.
The IPC resize path throws TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED: RATE_LIMITED when the resize bucket (16 burst, 16/s) is empty.
Reaping kills the PTY's process group and every /proc descendant of the recorded pid with SIGKILL, so closing a terminal also kills programs started inside it.
copyText accepts only a 1..128-char capsule-id-shaped string and otherwise throws ERR_CLIPBOARD_INVALID.
Broker caps: one write is at most 65536 decoded bytes; a shell-class session may emit 8388608 output bytes in total and an ai-class session 67108864; a wire line is at most 262144 bytes.
Shell-class sessions live at most 3600000 ms and ai-class sessions at most 14400000 ms before the broker closes them with reason SESSION_EXPIRED.

runBroker is the PTY engine: it admits open/write/resize/ack/close/pause/resume ops against owned spawn profiles, owns node-pty handles, accounts output credit per session, and emits open/data/exit/error events with a wire version and generation.

When cumulative output reaches the class byte cap the broker sends the final truncated chunk and closes the session with exit code 0 and reason SESSION_CAP. (inference) A full-screen agent CLI that repaints its whole input box per keystroke makes output grow with line length, so a very long typed line in a shell-class pair is a candidate way to reach 8388608 bytes.
If unacknowledged output exceeds 524288 bytes or 4096 frames the broker closes the session with exit code -1 and no reason; the renderer then shows the tile as exited.
A session older than its class lifetime is closed with exit code 0 and reason SESSION_EXPIRED, independent of user activity. (inference) This is a candidate for an exit that coincides with typing.
Input bytes are decoded with one shared fatal UTF-8 decoder and no streaming, so each write must be complete UTF-8; a write that splits a multi-byte character is refused as INVALID_INPUT.

handleWrite refuses WRITE_SHAPE for non-base64 input, WRITE_TOO_LARGE above 65536 bytes, INVALID_INPUT for non-UTF-8 bytes and WRITE_FAILED if node-pty write throws; for a live session terminalHost turns each into a fatal TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED frame.

handleOpen refuses SESSION_SHAPE, SESSION_DUPLICATE, SESSION_CLOSED, ADMISSION_SHAPE, SESSION_LIMIT (32 live), PROVIDER_SHAPE, COMMAND_SHAPE, UNKNOWN_PROVIDER, COMMAND_MISMATCH, CLASS_LIMIT (16 per class), DIMS_RANGE, SPAWN_BRAKE, SPAWN_SHAPE, SPAWN_FAILED, PTY_SHAPE and RECORD_FAILED.
A user close is staged: SIGHUP, wait 100 ms, SIGTERM, wait 250 ms, then SIGKILL and reap; internal faults (caps, pending overflow) skip the staging and SIGKILL directly.
Acks must advance monotonically and match the exact cumulative byte boundary of a sent frame; otherwise ACK_REFUSED.
The broker wire is versioned line-delimited JSON; the framer drops lines over 262144 bytes with LINE_TOO_LONG and non-object lines with MALFORMED without breaking the stream.
The IPC bridge binds fixed channels metaviewer:terminal.open, .attach, .close, .write, .resize, .ack and .capabilities; renderer values carrying exe, cwd, env, argv, path or channel are refused.

The IPC bridge write path re-checks WRITE_SHAPE and WRITE_TOO_LARGE, then TERMINAL_OWNER, BRIDGE_DISPOSED, ADMISSION_CONTEXT, SESSION_CLOSED/UNKNOWN_SESSION and TRANSPORT_FAILED, returning {ok:false,reason}.
The renderer facade returns {ok:false} with DISPOSED, NO_OWNER (before capabilities bootstrap) or INPUT_DISABLED (write before setEnabled(true)); main rechecks every effect.
SESSION_LIMIT, CLASS_LIMIT and SPAWN_BRAKE carry fixed operator remedy sentences that travel with error events to the renderer.
Env names that look like credentials never reach a PTY child, and loader/runtime variables (LD_*, DYLD_*, NODE_OPTIONS, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, PYTHON*) are scrubbed.
agentProviders.js builds host-owned agent CLI profiles (agent-codex, agent-gemini, agent-opencode, agent-muse) from binaries found on the host; renderer input never chooses the executable or argv.
A CLI that is missing or fails its environment checks is left out of the profile map; it is never replaced by a shell.

With MV_ARM64_CAPSULES=1 the host env is rebuilt from the OS account; an unclean HOME or XDG_RUNTIME_DIR throws AGENT_HOST_ENV_UNAVAILABLE, too many PATH segments AGENT_HOST_PATH_UNAVAILABLE, and in that mode no agent profile is offered.
The Muse profile runs inside unshare user/pid namespaces; without an unshare helper it throws AGENT_NAMESPACE_UNAVAILABLE and the profile is omitted.
MV_MUSE_RECORDING_UNSANDBOXED=1 is a host-only switch that adds --disable-sandbox to the Muse argv; it is never selected by renderer input.
terminalClient.js is the renderer end of a session port: it sequences input, checks output frames, and sends acks only after the terminal parser confirms it consumed the bytes.
Input over 65536 bytes is silently dropped: no error, no status, no chunking. Every accepted input increments inputSeq immediately, so several frames can be in flight before any host refusal returns.

On a retryable refusal the client rewinds inputSeq to expectedSeq-1 but does not resend the refused bytes; frames sent after the refused one and before this rewind still carry the old, now too-high sequence numbers. (inference) Those frames hit the host's fatal shape branch.
A non-retryable error frame or an exit frame ends the client; status becomes the raw error string (for example TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED) or 'Exited (<code>)'.
Out-of-order output, a frame over 65536 bytes, 256 pending frames, or extra keys end the client with 'Terminal stream refused'; a frame for another session ends it with 'Terminal binding refused'.

sideTerminalFacade.js adapts already-authorized session ports and host terminal methods to the side-terminal and deck shapes: a single-port facade, an empty-state facade, a broker opt-in facade, a fixed-API session transport and a multi-session port facade.
A binding with a malformed session id or no port throws 'Invalid terminal binding' (TERMINAL_BINDING_REFUSED); later use of a foreign or detached session throws 'Terminal binding refused'.

The deck's write path: createPortSessionFacade.write converts the byte array and calls client.input directly, or queues it until the port attaches; there is no chunking, size check or error reply on this path.
Any client status (error or exit) releases the session entry, closes the port and emits an exit event whose reason is the raw status text.
An ack that does not match a pending output credit throws 'Terminal credit refused' (TERMINAL_CREDIT_REFUSED).
The broker facade refuses open with TERMINAL_LAUNCH_UNAVAILABLE while disabled or busy, and setEnabled with TERMINAL_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE when the host has no opt-in or a toggle is in progress.
Side-terminal session outcomes are shown only as designed text 'Session ended.' or 'Session ended unexpectedly.'; host error strings and exit codes stay in data attributes.

The session transport throws TERMINAL_SESSION_INVALID, TERMINAL_ATTACH_FAILED (attach reply without a port), TERMINAL_RESIZE_REFUSED, TERMINAL_CLOSE_REFUSED, TERMINAL_PROVIDERS_UNAVAILABLE and TERMINAL_CLIPBOARD_UNAVAILABLE for bad requests or replies.
terminalDeckModel.js is the framework-free controller for the terminal deck: screens of terminal slots, launch, restart, close, paste, copy, acks, refusal formatting and the agent prompt gate.

Every deck input (xterm onData, paste fallback, Ctrl+C, custom CLI command, agent prompt) goes through writeSessionBytes, which returns true as soon as the bytes are handed to the facade, not when the host admits them.

On any session exit event the slot becomes status 'exited' (busy false); if the reason is not 'Exited (<n>)' the controller also asks the broker to close the session. The tile shows only the word 'exited' and a Restart button; the reason is not displayed.
The deck acknowledges each output frame as soon as it is delivered to listeners, using a cumulative byte count, before the xterm view has rendered it.

Open refusals are normalized by formatTerminalRefusal into '<CODE>: <hint>' using a fixed hint table (TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE, TERMINAL_DISABLED, SESSION_LIMIT, CLASS_LIMIT, SPAWN_BRAKE, RATE_LIMITED, DISPLAY_ONLY and others); unknown codes fall back to TERMINAL_OPEN_REFUSED.
launchProfile refuses an unknown profile with COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED: Selected terminal profile is unavailable (<id>). and a full deck with SESSION_LIMIT: All terminal screens are full.

prepareAgentPrompt polls agent output every 100 ms for up to 15000 ms; it pastes only after a known ready prompt and 300 ms of quiet, and otherwise fails with a toast such as 'Agent input prompt not observed within 15 seconds; nothing pasted.'
The workflow prompt is sent once as a bracketed paste (ESC[200~ ... ESC[201~) without Enter; the toast reads 'Prompt pasted into agent CLI — add your task; Enter was not sent.'

If the agent output shows a sign-in, API-key or workspace-trust question the prompt is never pasted: 'Complete authentication or workspace trust yourself, then choose the workflow again. Nothing pasted.'
Without an attested agent target, useWorkflowPrompt only copies the prompt to the clipboard ('Copied — paste into your agent CLI, not a shell.'); a shell never receives the workflow text.
Paste writes the whole clipboard text in one input; it reports pasted:true even though terminalClient silently drops inputs over 65536 bytes.
Closing a running slot sends Ctrl+C (0x03) before anything else, waits the close grace (150 ms default), then closes the broker session.
Agent output is kept per session as the last 32768 characters of escape-stripped text (at most 64 sessions) so the prompt gate can detect ready or authentication states.
Each xterm onData event (usually one keystroke when typing) becomes one writeSessionBytes call and therefore one sequenced input frame; nothing batches or throttles keystrokes in the renderer.
The deck shows workflow buttons 'Create automation', 'Run automation' and 'Direct task'; for a MicroVM pair only 'Direct task' is offered.

chooseWorkflow: with no matching pair it only copies the prompt; with a running agent profile it calls prepareAgentPrompt; otherwise it opens the 'Replace this paired process with an agent CLI:' chooser.
A MicroVM Direct task without a matching live binding shows 'MicroVM binding unavailable; nothing prepared.'
Opening a pair for the selected capsule shows 'Opening paired terminal…' and, on error, the raw error message or 'Paired terminal unavailable'.

Output frames are decoded per frame without stream mode, so a multi-byte character split across frames renders as replacement characters (inference); output for an unmounted tile is buffered up to 65536 characters.
pairedTerminals.js keeps one host-terminal slot per exact capsule id (or MicroVM workload id), reusing the deck controller's broker launch; reopening a pair keeps its live process.

A pair is reused only while its slot exists and is not exited and no new profile was chosen; otherwise the same slot is relaunched (reuseSlotId), so an exited paired shell comes back as a fresh process.
A pair target that is neither a valid capsule surface id nor a valid MicroVM context throws PAIRED_CAPSULE_INVALID (or WORKFLOW_MICROVM_CONTEXT from the MicroVM check).
Pair opens are serialized on one promise tail so two opens for the same capsule cannot launch two processes.
A new pair launches the 'shell' profile (shell class, 8388608-byte output cap and 3600000 ms lifetime in the broker) unless an agent profile was chosen.

workflowPrompts.js builds the fixed agent prompts for 'Create automation', 'Run automation' and 'Direct task'; Direct task points the agent at the docs/AGENT_ENTRY.md section 'Direct task' with a guard to release human control before acting and stop on rc 5 INPUT_UNCERTAIN, login or CAPTCHA.
A prompt with 40 or more lines, control characters or anything secret-shaped (Bearer, sk- keys, token/password/api_key assignments, data:image) throws WORKFLOW_PROMPT_UNSAFE.
A pasted identity line over 4096 chars, with control or bidi characters, or a malformed CAPSULE= or MICROVM= line throws WORKFLOW_IDENTITY_UNSAFE.
A MicroVM context must have exactly seven keys with profile guest-command-arm64-v1, backend firecracker and isa aarch64, else WORKFLOW_MICROVM_CONTEXT.
For a MicroVM only Direct task is allowed (WORKFLOW_MICROVM_KIND otherwise); an unknown kind throws WORKFLOW_PROMPT_KIND.
The MicroVM Direct task prompt embeds the binding as MV_TASK_BINDING JSON and a guard that the human alone owns Back and the agent must stop if the live binding changes.

agentPromptGate.js decides from escape-stripped agent output whether an agent CLI shows a known input prompt ('ready'), an authentication or trust question ('authentication') or neither ('waiting'); the start timeout is 15000 ms.
Authentication and trust questions take priority over ready markers, so a prompt is never pasted while the CLI is asking to sign in or trust a folder; the gate never answers those questions.
providers.js validates host-owned provider entries (at most 32 entries, argv 1..33 items of at most 4096 bytes) and builds a reference-only launch menu that leads with the System shell row.
A provider menu row is enabled only if the host reported available:true for that id; the shell row is disabled only on an explicit false.

Custom argv parsing returns errors 'Enter an executable.', 'The executable must not start with a dash.', 'Too many arguments (at most 32).', 'Arguments must not contain null bytes.' and 'One argument exceeds the size limit.'
TerminalView.vue renders one injected session port in xterm through terminalClient; mounting or disposing never spawns or kills a host session and the status line shows the client status text.
Each ResizeObserver callback posts a resize directly on the port; resizes beyond the host bucket (16 burst, 16/s) are retryable refusals that count toward the 64-refusal limit (inference).

BrokerLaunchControls.vue shows the 'Enable terminal access' opt-in and one launch button per host provider; outcomes are 'Terminal session opened.', 'TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE: terminal support is not bundled in this package', 'This terminal launch is unavailable.' or 'Terminal access is unavailable.'

SideTerminalOverlay.vue is the right-side terminal overlay on the kit SideTerminalPanel; data-terminal-state is TERMINAL_ATTACHED, TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE (no binding, empty-state facade) or TERMINAL_BINDING_REFUSED.
agentLane.js installs window.__agentLane, which returns an agent_lane/v1 snapshot of every [data-semantic-anchor] control (id, anchor, role, name, rect); it makes no host calls.

Installing twice throws ERR_AGENT_LANE_MOUNTED; a missing target or root throws ERR_AGENT_LANE_NO_TARGET or ERR_AGENT_LANE_NO_ROOT; fixture frame binding throws ERR_BENCH_FRAME_SHAPE, ERR_BENCH_FRAME_MOUNTED or ERR_BENCH_FRAME_NO_SNAPSHOT.
Every interactive control must carry both a stable id and a data-semantic-anchor; the strict gate throws ERR_AGENT_LANE_ANCHOR listing offenders.
AgentLaneHost.vue is a zero-DOM component that installs the __agentLane key on mount and removes it on unmount or when disabled.

identityForm.js holds pure form rules for the Identities dialog. They mirror the closed host validation in electron/preload.js, so a typo is explained in the form before the request is sent instead of coming back as a bare OPERATOR_PAYLOAD.

An identity id must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$ (2 to 40 characters) and must not be a protected name. Protected names are any mv- prefix plus the foreign names and prefixes in electron/identityProtection.js.
A display label must be non-empty, at most 128 code points, already trimmed, and free of control characters and the shell metacharacters ; ` $ | & < > \.
The allowed-sites list holds at most 16 hostnames. Each is at most 253 characters and matches a lower-case hostname pattern with no leading or trailing dot or dash.

The comma-separated Allowed sites field is split, trimmed, lower-cased, de-duplicated and sorted, and empty entries are dropped. The sort matters because the preload create check requires domains in strictly ascending order.

identityFormRequest returns the identity.create payload {id,label,domains}, or null when any rule fails. An empty display name falls back to the id. The dialog disables its Add identity button while this returns null.

Typed names are normalized on input: lower-cased, whitespace turned into dashes, and every other character outside a-z, 0-9 and dash removed. retainTypedIdentityName keeps the original spelling for the display-name placeholder.

identityErrorText maps host codes to operator text: IDENTITY_PROTECTED becomes "Managed outside MetaViewer (IDENTITY_PROTECTED)." and IDENTITY_BOUND becomes "This identity has an open capsule. Stop it first, then delete it."

PROFILE_NOT_PROVISIONED and PROFILE_MISSING say Docker profile provisioning failed: profiles/<id> must be private 0700 and owned by uid 10001, and the operator should check Docker access and the installed judge images (see docs/INSTALL.md#identity-store). The id is echoed only if it passes the id pattern; otherwise <id> is shown.

IDENTITY_REFUSED means the identity tool refused: the identity may be held by a running capsule or an open login view, or a native prerequisite is missing. OPERATOR_PAYLOAD means preload refused the request before the tool ran ("Check the id, label and domains.").

IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE means the identity tool could not run. The text tells the operator to set MV_SRF_BIN_DIR, MV_SRF_STATE_DIR and SRF_IDENTITY_STORE_ROOT and to point MV_OPERATOR_REPO at a checkout with tools/mv_identity.py. Any other code shows "The identity tool could not run: <code>", and an empty code shows the literal non-English fallback "AUSENTE — no reason supplied".

IdentitiesDialog.vue is the Identities modal. It lists saved identities and lets the operator add, delete, log in to, release and stop them, open one as human or as agent, and manage stored data. Identity calls go to props.host.identity (default operatorHost). Capsule mode calls go to globalThis.metaviewerRoles.

Each change of the open prop increments invocationGeneration, clears busy and login state, and lists again when the dialog opens. An invoke whose generation is stale returns without writing rows, errors or busy state, so a reply that arrives late after close and reopen is dropped.

invoke throws IDENTITY_HOST_ABSENT when the host exposes no identity API, and throws result.code when a host reply has ok false. The caught code goes through identityErrorText, so the operator sees mapped text in the alert line.

A request for a foreign identity (other projects or the live launcher) is refused in the renderer with IDENTITY_PROTECTED before any host call. Only one invoke runs at a time: a call made while busy returns at once.

If the role API choices() or programs() call throws after a successful list, the dialog keeps the rows it already had and shows "Capsule status is unavailable. Previously known states are retained; refresh Identities before opening another capsule."

Delete is refused for a protected identity (IDENTITY_PROTECTED) and for an open one (IDENTITY_BOUND). An identity counts as open when its mode row is busy, holds a surfaceId, or is in human or agent mode. deleteIdentity runs both checks again after the confirm dialog.
When a delete fails, its diagnostic is stored in failedDelete and shown again by the next list call, so the refresh after the failure does not clear the reason. A successful delete clears it.

Opening a Host program identity is refused in these cases. A lost capsule shows "Stop lost capsule before reopening this program." An open capsule in the other mode shows "This program is still open in <mode> mode. Stop the capsule before opening it in <role> mode." A missing saved binary or role API shows "Saved program binary unavailable. Open the program through Add capsule first."

A Host program open whose reply is not ok throws reply.code, or PROGRAM_OPEN_FAILED when there is no code. The alert shows the host reason when one is given, otherwise "Program could not be opened: <code>. Try Add capsule to check the program setup."

A browser identity is not opened by the dialog. It emits open-identity {profileId,role} and closes, and App.vue handles the event (openIdentityChoice). A Host program bound to an identity opens through roleApi.open. Otherwise it uses props.openProgram or roleApi.createProgram with {binary,role}, plus hostXpra when that is set.
Stop lost capsule calls roleApi.stop(surfaceId). A reply that is not ok raises its code, or CAPSULE_STOP_UNPROVEN when there is no code, and the code is shown through identityErrorText.

Release sends the holder that the last list call recorded to roleApi.releaseIdentity, and the tool checks it again. Any reply that is not ok raises IDENTITY_RELEASE_REFUSED, and the user sees "Release could not be verified. A live session or missing ownership evidence still holds this identity."

The dialog sets body[data-mv-modal] when it opens and no other modal holds the attribute. It removes the attribute only if this component set it, so other modals keep theirs. Native role views watch this attribute to hide while a modal is open.

The Stored data panel is blocked while the dialog is busy, while capsule modes are unknown (modesKnown is false during a role refresh), or while the selected identity is open. Saved slots therefore cannot change under a running capsule.

StoredDataSlots.vue manages the saved data slots of one profile: list, save, overwrite, load, copy to a new capsule, and delete. Every operation is one capsule_state_request/v0.2 sent through globalThis.metaviewer.slots.request, which is the preload slotRequest call.
With no slots API on the host, request throws SLOT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE. This code is not in the refusal map, so the user sees "Stored data is unavailable (SLOT_STORE_UNAVAILABLE). Refresh to retry."

The closed reason_code map covers SLOT_EXISTS, IDENTITY_BOUND, LOGIN_IN_PROGRESS, IDENTITY_PROTECTED, POLICY, SLOT_DISK_SPACE, SLOT_QUOTA, SLOT_LIST_LIMIT, SLOT_BUSY, SLOT_NOT_FOUND, SLOT_INCOMPATIBLE, SLOT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and SLOT_QUARANTINED, each with fixed text. Any other code shows "Stored data is unavailable (<code or SLOT_OPERATION_FAILED>). Refresh to retry."
A list reply whose event is not completed throws its reason_code. A completed list with no slots array throws SLOT_LIST_MISSING.

Slot names and copy destinations must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$. A copy destination must also differ from the source and must not be protected or foreign. The user sees "Use 2–40 lowercase letters, numbers and dashes for the slot name." or "Choose a new capsule name using lowercase letters, numbers and dashes."

Every action is refused while the parent marks the panel blocked, or while the profile is protected or foreign. A watch on [profileId, blocked] clears all local state and lists again, so the panel never shows rows from another profile.

After a write completes, the list is read again. If that read fails, the success text is kept and the refusal is added after it, so the user still sees that the write happened and does not press Save twice.

Every operation needs a confirm dialog that warns "Signed-in sessions travel with stored data". While it runs, the status line shows "<Verb> <slot>… Keep MetaViewer open until this finishes." A finished copy emits changed and copied(destination), and IdentitiesDialog then lists again and selects the new profile.

identityProtection.js is the shared list of identities that MetaViewer must never delete or drive: names owned by other projects or by the live launcher. The comment says it must stay in sync with protected_identity in tools/mv_identity.py.

An id is foreign when it starts with srf-id-cuentas-, srf-id-perplexity- or srf-pg-, or when it is in PROTECTED_HOLDERS (7 fixed names). An id is protected when it is foreign or starts with mv-. Protected ids cannot be created or deleted from the UI. Foreign ids also cannot be opened, logged in to, released or given stored data.

Callers: IdentitiesDialog.vue, StoredDataSlots.vue, identityForm.js, and in the main process authorityWire.js, roleHost.js, operatorBridge.js and openingMode.js. Renderer and host therefore apply the same list.
