identityMarkers.js stores login confirmation markers, one <profile>.json per profile, in a directory separate from the opaque browser profiles. roleHost.js creates it on <userData or MV_SRF_STATE_DIR>/identity-markers, and the Last login line in Identities comes from it.

read throws IDENTITY_MARKER_REFUSED unless the file is a regular file (opened with O_NOFOLLOW), owned by the current uid, mode exactly 0600, at most 1024 bytes, with schema metaviewer.login_confirmation/v0.3, a matching profile_id, source operator and a positive integer confirmed_unix_ms. A missing file returns null, and the dialog shows "Not recorded".

confirm requires the marker directory to be a real directory (not a symlink), owned by the current uid and mode 0700. It writes a 0600 temporary file with wx and fsyncs it, then renames it into place. Only the confirm-login op calls it, and roleHost refuses that op unless the surface is human-controlled (LOGIN_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRES_HUMAN).

A profile name that does not match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$ throws IDENTITY_MARKER_REFUSED before any filesystem access, which blocks path traversal. When the role host catches a read failure it sets markerError to IDENTITY_MARKER_REFUSED, and the dialog prints that code in the Last login line.

profilePicker.js chooses the browser profile for each later Add capsule create. It is pure and injected, with no filesystem, process, network or Electron access. It returns either a surface_request/v0.2 create or a typed refusal, and every refusal fails closed.

Only one capsule creation runs per host state map. acquireCapsuleCreation returns null while a creation is already in progress, otherwise a release function that is safe to call twice. authorityWire.js, roleHost.js and main.js share it.

pickProfile checks in this order: bad input gives PICKER_INPUT_INVALID; 16 or more live surfaces give CAPSULE_LIMIT_REACHED; free memory below 6 GiB (4 GiB RAM plus 2 GiB shm), or unreadable memory, gives RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED; no unbound profile gives NO_FREE_PROFILE; an identity list that cannot be read gives IDENTITY_LIST_UNAVAILABLE; and no free profile with an existing identity gives NO_IDENTITY, which lists the missing ids.

Destroyed and lost surfaces do not count toward the live limit. A lost browser surface still keeps its profile bound until an explicit destroy proves the release. A live surface with no readable profile_id still counts toward the limit.

Candidates are the browser-kind keys of the MV_SRF_PROFILES JSON map (at most 1048576 bytes), with MV_SRF_LIVE_PROFILE placed at the head. A missing or malformed map falls back to the single live profile, or mv-live-1 when that is unset. Non-browser kinds are filtered out.

authorityWire.js createSurface calls pickCreateRequest with the live capsule states, listIdentities and a host memory reader. A throwing memory probe becomes null, which means a refusal. A throwing or not-ok identity list becomes null and gives IDENTITY_LIST_UNAVAILABLE. Neither failure falls back silently.

When memory is short, the user sees "Not enough free host memory (<x.x> GiB available; one capsule needs 6 GiB: 4 GiB RAM + 2 GiB shm; <n> of 16 open). Close an open capsule or other applications and try again." When the memory probe cannot be read, the text says no capsule was started and asks the operator to check the probe and restart MetaViewer.

refusalReply returns {ok:false, code, message, action}. NO_IDENTITY and IDENTITY_LIST_UNAVAILABLE carry the action {id:open-identities}, labelled "Create identity…" or "Open Identities…", which opens the Identities dialog. An unknown code becomes PICKER_INPUT_INVALID.

CREATE_REFUSAL_REASONS gives an operator sentence for every create-path code, including SURFACE_CREATE_BUSY, SURFACE_CREATE_TIMEOUT, SURFACE_CREATE_FAILED, ADAPTER_SETUP, ADAPTER_ERROR and DISPLAY_ONLY. createRefusalReason names the missing profile for NO_IDENTITY (default mv-live-2) and returns "This request is unavailable. Please try again." for unknown codes.

VM profiles are offered only when arch is arm64. Each needs Kind and NativeKind vm, Program notepad-vm, mode agent, integer Width and Height from 1 to 8192, a Display like :N, and an absolute RAMRoot. If more than 16 qualify, the result is empty.

recordingModel.js is the pure model for the recording panel (AC-07). It defines the phase vocabularies, the record-to-disk gates, the typed refusal copy, and stable DOM ids and anchors. Captures live in RAM. The host owns every sink, and this module never touches disk, network or clipboard.

Record phases are idle, starting, recording, stopping, sealed and error. Screenshot states are idle, capturing, done and error. Unknown values normalize to idle, so a hostile or unknown phase renders idle and is never treated as recording.

Export to disk is possible only when the host advertises a destination, which must be a non-empty string with no surrounding whitespace, and the recording is sealed. A missing destination is checked before the seal (ERR_EXPORT_WITHOUT_DESTINATION, "No export destination advertised by the host"). An unsealed recording is refused next (ERR_EXPORT_UNSEALED_RECORDING, "Only sealed recordings can be exported").

The per-row gate uses a different order from the panel gate: unavailable, then sealed-required, then destination-required. An unsealed row with no destination therefore shows "Sealed required", while the panel refusal row shows the missing destination.

The closed host export refusal codes are DESTINATION_UNSET, CAPTURE_UNKNOWN, NOT_SEALED, DESTINATION_UNAVAILABLE, DESTINATION_EXISTS, LIMIT, NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY and CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE. An unknown code normalizes to CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE. The raw code appears only in the data-export-code attribute, never in visible text.

Visible export refusal text: "No export destination advertised by the host", "Only sealed recordings can be exported", "Export destination is unavailable", "Recording already exported" (DESTINATION_EXISTS), "Export limit reached" (LIMIT). Every other code, including CAPTURE_UNKNOWN and NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY, shows "Recording is unavailable".

Capture refusal text covers SURFACE_UNKNOWN, ALREADY_RECORDING, NOT_RECORDING, CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE ("no frame has arrived yet, or the host did not answer"), NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY, LIMIT, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, POLICY and RECORDING_FAILED. Any other non-empty code shows "Capture failed.", and an empty code shows nothing.

RECORDING_FAILED is a local code that the capture store records when the host reports the error phase. It never travels on the wire. ui/src/capture/capturePort.js imports it together with MV_RECORDING_PHASES.

The frame-rate field accepts an empty value (host default) or a plain integer from 1 to 60. Anything else is invalid and never reaches the host. The hint says a higher choice does not add frames, because the live source delivers only a few frames per second.

A host id is used as-is in DOM ids and anchors only if it is a canonical lower-case dash id that does not start with encoded-. Otherwise every UTF-16 unit is hex-encoded between encoded- and -end, so an encoded value can never collide with a real host id.
An unreadable elapsed value renders "--:--" and an unreadable counter renders "Unknown", never a made-up zero. A TTL of zero or less renders "Expired".

The manifest takes the store rows whose kind is recording and whose surface_id is this surface, and converts duration_ms to whole seconds. The screenshot list (captureShotsFor) takes kind shot rows only when sealed is true and the phase is sealed. captureEntryFor rejects __proto__, constructor and prototype as surface ids.

MvRecordingPanel.vue is the per-capsule recording panel: a Record for AI toggle, a Screenshot button, a frame-rate field, the RAM recordings manifest and a sealed screenshots list, each with an export gated on destination and seal. App.vue mounts it with capture-state and capture-available. Without a store it emits kit submit-intent payloads instead.

With a store bound, the toggle calls captureState.toggleRecord(capsuleId), and only a start adds {maxFps} when the field is valid. An ok reply that carries a recording sets the receipt "Sealed N frames, M dropped." A rejected promise becomes {ok:false, code:CAPTURE_UNAVAILABLE}.

The toggle is disabled with a reason in its tooltip and data-unavailable-reason: "Recording is unavailable" when unavailableReason is set or the capture is held (store bound but captureAvailable false), "Recording is starting/stopping" during a transition, or "Frame rate must be a whole number from 1 to 60" when the frame-rate value is invalid. An invalid frame rate blocks a start but never a stop.
The last refusal code the store recorded for the capsule (lastCode) is shown as a status line with the code in data-error-code. Before this, a refused click looked like a dead button.

Export guards against double clicks in the same tick by checking the live status map synchronously and setting exporting before the async call. A row that is already exporting or exported does nothing. Only an ok reply with a 64-hex sha256 renders "Exported <8-hex digest prefix>". Every other reply renders the typed refusal.
Export outcomes are kept per display row id in a local reactive Map. The map is cleared when the store or the capsule changes, so a new capsule never shows another capsule's export state.

Earlier, sealed recordings were never listed and the panel kept saying "No recordings yet." Now the panel calls store.refresh(capsuleId) on mount (only for a listable store with no rows for this capsule), on every capsule switch, and on a swap to an empty listable store. Refresh errors are swallowed.

A row id that is non-canonical or duplicated is shown as unknown-<index>, and its select and export controls are disabled. A screenshot whose id collides with a recording gets the display id <id>-shot. Shot export status is keyed shot:<id>, so DOM ids stay unique across both tables.

The panel-level refusal row shows "No export destination advertised by the host" (data-refusal-code ERR_EXPORT_WITHOUT_DESTINATION) when no destination is configured, or "Recording is unavailable" (ERR_RECORDING_UNAVAILABLE) when unavailableReason is set. A row in the error phase shows "Recording failed" with data-error-code ERR_RECORDING_FAILED.

recordingClock.js interpolates the elapsed readout between sparse host capture events. It starts from the last host elapsed_ms and adds local monotonic time, never wall-clock time alone and never a made-up zero.

If a host sample is at most 1000 ms (MV_ELAPSED_JITTER_MS) behind the shown value, the readout holds the shown value instead of stepping back. A larger lag snaps to the host value. The display tick is 1000 ms.
While recording, elapsed is interpolated from the anchor. In every other phase, the host elapsedMs is shown as reported, or null (rendered "--:--") when it is unusable.

The panel shows a fixed note: "Measured on the reference host: the live tile delivered about 2 frames per second (capture 318 to 567 ms per frame)." The hint in recordingModel.js says about 2.7 fps for the same source, so the two comments disagree.

useRecordingElapsed is a Vue composable that returns a computed elapsed in ms, or null. A local interval runs only while the phase is recording and is cleared in any other phase and when the scope is disposed. The clock (now, setInterval, clearInterval, tickMs) can be injected so tests run deterministically.

The watcher watches one string key, phase|elapsedMs, with flush sync, so the local time is stamped as soon as a host event is seen. The timer handle is unref-ed when possible, so it never keeps a Node test process alive.

recordingBadgeCopy builds the tile badge text: the phase word, "Recording mm:ss" while recording, and " — <reason>" when a capture action was refused. The phase checks have no error branch, so an error phase shows "Idle" followed by the RECORDING_FAILED reason when the store set that code.

RecordingBadge.vue is meant as a drop-in for the badge span of wall/TileCaptureChrome.vue, keeping the same id, anchor, classes, role and data-variant. On this commit grep finds it imported only by tests (recstate-badge, recstate-panel), not by any production component.

humanTrace.js records human_trace/v0.3 rows (schema metaviewer.human_trace/v0.3) for click, move, key and scroll events on a human tile. It maps tile coordinates to capsule coordinates and writes one JSON line per event to a synchronous sink.

Every printable key is withheld. A key event keeps its name only when it is a navigation key AND the AX context explicitly says not sensitive and not a password. A missing AX row counts as sensitive, and the row is marked redacted.

record throws TRACE_EVENT_REFUSED, TRACE_LIMIT, TRACE_CLOCK_REFUSED, TRACE_GEOMETRY_REFUSED, TRACE_COORDINATE_REFUSED, TRACE_BUTTON_REFUSED, TRACE_KEY_PHASE_REFUSED or TRACE_SCROLL_REFUSED. createHumanTrace throws TRACE_BINDING_REFUSED for ids outside [a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]{1,128}. When the trace is inactive, record returns false without writing.

The trace file is human-trace-<uuid>.jsonl under <destination>/<profileId>, opened with O_EXCL and O_NOFOLLOW at mode 0600 in a directory with mode 0700. The default byte limit is 50 MiB, shared through one budget object, and retention defaults to 14 days. roleHost.js creates the file only for a human role and refuses with TRACE_DESTINATION_UNSET when MV_RECORDING_DESTINATION is unset.

When the byte budget would be exceeded, the trace pauses for good (budget.paused), calls onPause once and drops later events. roleHost then sets the view state recording to paused_size_limit. A short write throws TRACE_WRITE_FAILED, and a write after close throws TRACE_CLOSED.

Pruning deletes only regular files named human-trace-*.jsonl, owned by the current uid and older than the retention days, one level into profile directories. The root must be owned by the current uid, have no group or other permission bits, and not be a symlink, or pruning throws TRACE_DIRECTORY_REFUSED. A retention below 1 throws TRACE_RETENTION_REFUSED.

Two sinks exist. createHumanTraceBuffer keeps lines in memory (4 MiB default, TRACE_LIMIT on overflow) and exports with no-clobber wx, deleting the partial file on failure. createHumanTraceFile writes each event to disk at once instead of exporting when the tile closes. roleHost.js uses the file sink.

activityModel.js turns reported authority outcomes (intent acks, action_verdict admissions and refusals, transport refusals and human-input refusals) into closed, frozen rows for the activity strip. Its text is a local copy of the core/hostAdapters.js literals, so the strip never trusts a message received as a prop.
The strip keeps at most 8 entries. App.vue enforces the same limit inline (ACTIVITY_LIMIT = 8, using slice(-8)) so stub harnesses never need this module, and a test pins both literals.

Human-input refusal codes NOT_IN_CONTROL, INPUT_MODE_READ, SURFACE_UNKNOWN, STALE_STREAM, LIMIT, NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY, SCHEMA and CORE_UNAVAILABLE render as "Input refused: <reason> (<CODE>)." Repeated identical refusals are merged into one row with a "×N" suffix.

normalizeActivityEntry checks in this order. 1: input refusals. 2: the NO_IDENTITY variants (NO_IDENTITY__X, NO_IDENTITY:id or missingId), which name the missing profile. 3: an UPPER_SNAKE code with a safe reason of at most 256 characters, rendered "<CODE>: <reason>" (codes starting ERR_ or LAYOUT_ excluded). 4: the closed ACTIVITY_ROWS map. 5: any other UPPER_SNAKE code, rendered as "<CODE>: This request is unavailable. Please try again." 6: anything else, the generic text.

ACTIVITY_ROWS gives fixed text for success codes (INTENT_ACKNOWLEDGED "Request sent.", ACTION_ADMITTED "Action admitted."), verdict refusals (STALE_FRAME, SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED, LOCKED_BY_OTHER, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, OUT_OF_BOUNDS, POLICY) and create-path refusals, which repeat the profilePicker copy. CAPTCHA_HANDOFF hands a bot check to the human: "CAPTCHA or bot check: solve it in the capsule, then re-run".
A feed item with no positive safe-integer seq, or one that is not an object, returns null and is not rendered.
The total is the largest valid seq, because App.vue assigns seq values one after another from 1. Once more than 8 outcomes have been recorded, the count reads "latest 8 of N".

ActivityStrip.vue is a docked bar below the wall with an Activity toggle, a count, and a role=log list of the newest outcomes (data-activity-type, data-activity-tone). It takes props and emits nothing. App.vue mounts it with :entries="activityFeed".
The strip takes the last 8 feed items and normalizes each through normalizeActivityEntry. Null entries are dropped, so the number shown can be lower than 8 even when the feed is full.

The list renders only when it is expanded and has rows. Collapsed or empty, the bar shows only the count and "No authority activity yet.". The li for the empty state inside the list can never render, because the list requires rows.length.

activity.css uses kit tokens only, with no color literals or remote imports. The bar sits in the shell grid, so it resizes the wall instead of covering tiles. The open list is fixed at 132px tall and scrolls inside. Row tone sets a 6px status dot through [data-activity-tone='refusal'].

App.vue recordActivity is the only writer of the activity feed. It drops calls while the host is inactive, assigns seq values one after another, keeps a reason only when it is 1 to 256 characters with no control characters, and keeps the last 8 entries.

App.vue mounts IdentitiesDialog unless the wall is a display-only nested wall. It passes before-delete=forgetIdentityLayout and open-program=createProgramCapsule, and routes open-identity to openIdentityChoice.

ui/electron/main.js is the Electron main entry (unit W0-SHELL-MAIN): it owns the window lifecycle, default-deny navigation and permission policy, top-frame sender admission for privileged IPC, serving the bundled renderer under app://metaviewer with a strict CSP, retail launch guards, the fuse table and supervision of the core connection and the daemon adapter.

mainDirectEntry runs only when Electron loads main.js directly: it validates argv/env with validateRetailLaunch, requires Electron 44.9.2 (ELECTRON_PIN), registers the privileged app scheme before any await, loads host bindings with loadMainBindings, then calls bootProductionMain and prints METAVIEWER_MAIN_READY.

A boot failure is shown as a non-modal warning dialog titled 'MetaViewer could not start' with message '<CODE>: MetaViewer could not start.'; an ADAPTER_* code adds 'The surface runtime could not start. Check the adapter installation and MV_SRF_BIN_DIR configuration, then restart MetaViewer...', anything else adds 'Check the installation and the startup error in the host logs, then restart MetaViewer.' Raw host diagnostics never enter the dialog; only a code matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,63}$ is shown.

failClosed prints the error to stderr, then (except for RETAIL_FLAG and RETAIL_ENV, which exit before readiness) waits for app ready, shows the startup dialog, waits for it to close or 15000 ms, and exits with app.exit(1).

When the core is missing (no owner-only socket, bad MV_CORE_CONFIG, failed hello), loadMainBindings converts every acquisition failure into MainError CORE_SEAMS_ABSENT with message 'trusted host bindings unavailable (<cause>)', where cause is a closed token such as SOCKET_PATH, CONFIG_OPEN or HELLO_TIMEOUT; only SETTINGS_DESTINATION and SETTINGS_IN_REPO pass through unchanged. The user then sees the 'MetaViewer could not start' dialog and the app exits.

MV_CORE_BOOTSTRAP may replace ./hostBindings.js with another host module, but only as an absolute, NUL-free path to a regular, non-symlink file owned by the current uid with no group/other permission bits (checked before and after realpath); the module must export createMainBindings and return a core with start/request/dispose/getStatus and wire.frames.subscribe.

The daemon adapter launcher is created only when MV_ADAPTER_BIN is non-empty and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is absolute; it gets shutdownTimeoutMs ADAPTER_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS (45000 ms), set above the adapter's own 30 s close budget so SIGKILL does not land mid-destroy, and its stderr lines are redacted before printing.

bootProductionMain refuses before any window exists: retail refusal codes from validateRetailLaunch, ELECTRON_PIN when the running Electron is not 44.9.2, and SINGLE_INSTANCE ('another instance holds the lock') after calling app.quit().

In a non-nested launch the core must reach availability 'live' or boot unwinds and throws CORE_UNAVAILABLE ('core did not reach live'); this happens before the BrowserWindow is constructed, so refused core readiness leaves zero windows.

MV_HEADLESS_ONLY=1 with an invalid MicroVM profile throws HEADLESS_PROFILE_INVALID ('The configured MicroVM profile is invalid.'); headless mode with no adapter throws ADAPTER_ABSENT ('The configured MicroVM requires the daemon adapter.').

If MV_SRF_BIN_DIR is set (or headless mode) and the adapter is not live with handshakeSeen, boot prints METAVIEWER_BOOT_REFUSED and throws an ADAPTER_* code (ADAPTER_OPENSUPERFICIES_ABSENT, ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE, ADAPTER_DEGRADED or ADAPTER_START_FAILED) with text telling the user to check MV_SRF_LIVE_PROFILE / MV_SRF_LIVE_RAM_ROOT or unset MV_SRF_BIN_DIR for core-only. Without MV_SRF_BIN_DIR a failed adapter leaves a core-only wall.

With a live adapter and outside MicroVM/ARM64 capsule mode, boot reserves a pending:<profile> entry in capsuleStates and fires exactly one asynchronous boot-time capsule create; the window is built without waiting for it.

requestFirstSurfaceCreate refuses with SURFACE_CREATE_BUSY when another creation holds the slot and RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED when /proc/meminfo free memory is unreadable or below CAPSULE_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES; any failure is normalised to a SURFACE_CREATE_* code, logged as METAVIEWER_SURFACE_CREATE_DEGRADED, and the window is kept.

The boot-time capsule create defaults to kind browser, geometry 1280x900 and profile mv-live-1; MV_SRF_LIVE_PROFILE and the JSON map MV_SRF_PROFILES (up to 1048576 chars) can override profile, kind, size (1..16384) and nested_depth (desktop_capsule only); a malformed map falls back to the defaults.

A failed boot-time capsule create shows the dialog 'MetaViewer could not open the first capsule' with 'The wall is still available...' guidance (RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED, ADAPTER_*, or open Identities); IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE is suppressed because the Identities row and the renderer refusal notice already cover it.

Only the two layout channels are registered directly by main: metaviewer:layout.load (no arguments) and metaviewer:layout.save (one string). Each listener begins with observeSender and throws MainError with the sender code, then LAYOUT_BOUNDS on the wrong argument count, then decodes and invokes. All other channels come from bridge modules (authorityWire, operatorBridge, captureBridge, capturePreferencesBridge, frameDiag, displayReader, qaAnchors, roleHost).

observeSender admits an IPC call only from the one expected webContents, not destroyed, whose sending frame is the main frame by strict object identity and whose origin is app://metaviewer and URL a canonical bundled URL; it returns frozen refusals SENDER, FRAME_NULL, FRAME_DETACHED, SUBFRAME, FRAME_ORIGIN or FRAME_URL and never throws.

Window policy is default-deny: every window.open is denied, permission request and check handlers always deny, webview attach is prevented, and navigation/redirect/frame-navigation is cancelled unless decideNavigation allows a canonical app://metaviewer URL. The only exception opens exactly https://github.com/oguirado/MetaViewer externally through shell.openExternal (the Settings Source link).

validateRetailLaunch refuses ARGV_SHAPE (more than 256 items, item over 4096 chars or NUL), ENV_SHAPE, RETAIL_FLAG for debug/inspect/require/remote-debugging/--no-sandbox flags, RETAIL_ENV for forbidden environment names or for MV_E2E_LIVE/MV_FRAME_DIAG in a packaged build (or values other than '1' / '0'/'1').

validateRetailLaunch also refuses NESTED_DEPTH for any --nested-depth form other than exactly --nested-depth=1 or for repeating it, and UNKNOWN_SWITCH for any dash-led argument except --user-data-dir and --ozone-platform; --nested-depth=1 switches main to display-only nested mode.

createRendererReadyGate prints METAVIEWER_RENDERER_READY only after three witnesses: the index document was served with status 200, did-finish-load fired, and the preload sent an argument-free metaviewer:renderer-ready from an admitted top frame at app://metaviewer/index.html; any other ping throws RENDERER_READY.

createLayoutBridge stores the layout at <userData>/presentation/layout.json (directory mode 0700, outside the source tree), validates text up to 256 KiB with the kit decoder for scope metaviewer/default/main-wall or the metaviewer.desktops/v1 desktop state, and throws LAYOUT_CONTRACT_ABSENT or LAYOUT_CONTRACT_INVALID.
Layout save is atomic: it writes a random temporary file with mode 0600 (exclusive create), fsyncs it, renames it over layout.json, fsyncs the directory and always removes the temporary file.

admitBridge throws BRIDGE_PARITY unless the injected bridge is exactly two {channel,decode,invoke} entries naming metaviewer:layout.load and metaviewer:layout.save once each, so main and preload channel literals cannot drift.
After the window loads, main pushes adapter status to the renderer on metaviewer:adapter-status (initial snapshot and every later onStatus transition); send failures during teardown are ignored.

Main installs the operator bridge (identity, egress, handoff and demo buttons), then capture preferences and capture bridges, then the authority wire with capsuleStates, clipboard and identity listing, all with the same observeSender admission; none of these are installed in nested mode.
If the window's renderer process dies (render-process-gone for the authority contents) the app quits rather than keep an interactive window; child-process-gone only logs METAVIEWER_PROCESS_GONE.
Ctrl+Q (no Alt/Shift/Meta) quits through the normal will-quit disposal; will-quit is prevented once, dispose() unwinds every bridge, window, scheme, adapter and core, then app.quit() runs again.

unwind hides the window before anything else so a slow bridge teardown (a demo recording stop can wait up to 10 s) never leaves a frozen window on screen, then removes IPC handlers in reverse order and disposes bridges, window, scheme, adapter and core.

When the core reports the session journal is full, main shows a warning 'Session journal full' / 'This session has reached its journal limit.' with detail 'New work is refused. Capsules are stopping in order...' or, for JOURNAL_STOP_FAILED, 'A capsule could not be stopped. Stop the remaining capsules before starting a new session.'

ui/electron/coreLauncher.js holds two single-flight child supervisors: createCoreLauncher (a native core child with environment allowlist, bounded stdio and authenticated handshake) and createAdapterLauncher (the bundled daemon adapter that may degrade to core-only), plus environment scrubbing, the kill guard and headless-profile checks.

On this commit the production main does not spawn the core: hostBindings.createMainBindings attaches to an already running core socket and supplies a core object whose start() just returns its status; createCoreLauncher is exercised by tests (for example ui/test/coreLauncher.test.js) (inference from importers).

createCoreLauncher.request throws NOT_LIVE when not live, REQUEST_SHAPE when the message cannot be JSON-measured, REQUEST_BYTES over maxRequestBytes, QUEUE_FULL or QUEUE_BYTES when in-flight limits are exceeded, and REQUEST_TIMEOUT after requestTimeoutMs; a failed request never resends and the launcher stays live.

Core start never throws: spawn, connect and hello failures set availability 'unavailable' with reasons such as 'core spawn failed', 'core handshake failed: connect refused', 'core handshake failed: VERSION_MISMATCH' or 'bad authority epoch', and the launcher never respawns.
Core limits are exact positive safe integers; handshakeTimeoutMs above 10000 is refused with LIMITS ('handshakeTimeoutMs exceeds the startup budget').

The core child environment is an exact allowlist (LANG, LC_ALL, PATH, TMPDIR, TZ) plus the validated runtime dir; names starting with DYLD_, ELECTRON_, LD_, NODE_ or PYTHON and BASH_ENV/ENV/GCONV_PATH/HOSTALIASES/ZDOTDIR are forbidden, and findForbiddenEnv feeds the RETAIL_ENV launch refusal.

validateKillTarget allows signals only to a safe-integer pid greater than 1 that is neither the caller pid nor its process group; teardown sends SIGTERM, waits shutdownTimeoutMs for exit evidence, then SIGKILL and waits again.

The adapter preflight degrades with ADAPTER_ABSENT when the adapter binary path is not absolute, missing or not executable, and with OPENSUPERFICIES_ABSENT when MV_SRF_BIN_DIR is not an absolute existing directory; a valid guest-command or headless profile skips the MV_SRF_BIN_DIR check.

A degraded adapter carries a user message, for example 'Degraded mode (OPENSUPERFICIES_ABSENT): OpenSuperficies (MV_SRF_BIN_DIR) is absent; capsules are unavailable and MetaViewer is running core-only.' or the ADAPTER_CRASHED form that includes the redacted last stderr line.
Adapter defaults: 65536-byte stdout line and stderr tail, 5000 ms handshake, 2000 ms shutdown wait (main overrides shutdown to 45000 ms); handshake over 10000 ms is refused with LIMITS.

The default adapter handshake succeeds when $XDG_STATE_HOME/metaviewer/sessions/$MV_SESSION_ID/events/1.json exists and is non-empty or when the adapter prints the stdout line ADAPTER_HANDSHAKE_OK; it polls every 20 ms and throws ADAPTER_EXITED or ADAPTER_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT.

redactAdapterDiagnostic keeps only the last 8192 chars and replaces values of env keys matching token/secret/password/credential/proxy, key=value credentials and URL userinfo with [REDACTED] before any adapter text is printed or retained.

requireHeadlessMode returns false unless MV_HEADLESS_ONLY=1, and throws HEADLESS_PROFILE_INVALID when the protected MV_HEADLESS_PROFILE file (arm64 only, owner-only, single link, at most 65536 bytes, schema mv-headless-host/v1) cannot be verified, so headless mode never falls back to graphical startup.

ui/electron/hostBindings.js is the default host module behind loadMainBindings: createMainBindings attaches to the running owner-only core socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/metaviewer/core.sock using the UI registration and core hello pinned in MV_CORE_CONFIG, and returns the core handle plus the wire (frames, terminals, display, capture, rewind, guest command, headless).

Acquisition fails closed with CORE_SEAMS_ABSENT tagged by step: CONFIG_ENV (MV_CORE_CONFIG or XDG_RUNTIME_DIR missing or relative), RUNTIME_DIRECTORY (runtime dirs not 0700 owned by the user), SOCKET_PATH (core.sock missing, not a socket or not 0600), then CONFIG_OPEN/READ/VALIDATE for the pinned config.

MV_CORE_CONFIG must be a regular user-owned file of at most 1 MiB, not group/other writable, with a valid session_id, a core hello/v0.2 registration and exactly one ui peer whose hello names component_commit as 40 hex chars.

The socket peer is authenticated before any hello is sent: SO_PEERCRED uid must equal the current uid and the kernel peer VFS inode must match the lstat inode of core.sock; PEER_NOT_READY is retried every 25 ms within the hello timer, other failures shut down with the closed cause token.
readPeerCredentials runs a fixed /usr/bin/python3 probe with a 3000 ms timeout and raises PEER_NOT_READY (exit 75), PEER_PROBE_TIMEOUT or PEER_PROBE_IO.

After the hello the socket path is re-checked (SOCKET_CHANGED if inode, device, mode or uid changed); the connection is never reconnected and a list request is sent every 10000 ms as keepalive because the transport closes idle peers after 30 s.

When the core ends the session journal, every surface is published as 'lost', in-flight requests reject with JOURNAL_FULL ('Session journal is full; start a new session.') and onSessionEnd triggers main's 'Session journal full' dialog once (again for JOURNAL_STOP_FAILED).

Surface creates are serialised: a second create while one is pending throws SURFACE_CREATE_BUSY, and a create rejects with SURFACE_CREATE_TIMEOUT after SURFACE_CREATE_DEADLINE_MS (60000 ms); METAVIEWER_SURFACE_CREATE_SENT is printed only from the socket write callback.

stopSurface throws CAPSULE_STOP_REFUSED or CAPSULE_STOP_TIMEOUT after 90000 ms; switchRole throws CAPSULE_MODE_REFUSED (bad id/role, surface not active, journal ended, pending switch) or CAPSULE_MODE_TIMEOUT after 30000 ms.

validateSurfaceCreateRequest admits only surface_request/v0.2 op create with kind browser, desktop_capsule, game_capsule or vm, a profile_id matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$, integer geometry 1..16384 and nested_depth 0/1 only for desktop_capsule; anything else throws SURFACE_CREATE_INVALID.

createProfileRefusal turns an adapter create error whose detail says 'profile already bound' into SURFACE_PROFILE_BOUND and 'remains quarantined' or 'unresolved native outcome' into SURFACE_PROFILE_QUARANTINED so the renderer can bring the existing tile back.

ui/electron/operatorBridge.js is the host-only operator seam: identity list/show/create/delete/login through the mv_identity.py tool, per-identity egress records, handoff notifications from run directories, and the demo/entry buttons; it registers no agent channel or credential operation.

installOperatorBridge registers one ipcMain.handle per OPERATOR_METHODS entry as metaviewer:<method>, each refusing with OPERATOR_SENDER when disposed or when observeSender does not admit the caller, and pushes metaviewer:handoff.state and metaviewer:demo.state to the renderer; handoff discovery refreshes every 1000 ms.

identityRunner spawns python3 with a fixed argv and a fixed environment allowlist (never a shell); it fails with IDENTITY_TIMEOUT after 30000 ms (1800000 ms for login), IDENTITY_LIMIT over 65536 output bytes, LOGIN_URL when the announced login view is not loopback http, and LOGIN_VIEW when it cannot be opened.

Identity replies are closed: IDENTITY_PROTECTED, PROFILE_MISSING, PROFILE_NOT_PROVISIONED and IDENTITY_BOUND pass through, other tool refusals become IDENTITY_REFUSED, and a tool that cannot run maps to IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE; foreign or protected ids are refused before spawning.

egress.set refuses NET_OPEN_PREREQ when open mode is not supported by the adapter without confirm:true, NET_PROXIED_UNSUPPORTED for allowlisted mode without proxied support, and any I/O failure as NET_EGRESS_IO; records are written under MV_SRF_STATE_DIR/egress and take effect on the next capsule start.

handoff.list and handoff.ack return HANDOFF_UNAVAILABLE when MV_HANDOFF_PATHS is malformed or no latched record matches the surface_id and step_index; an ack writes a metaviewer.handoff_ack/v1 file next to the record.

Handoff discovery is bounded (scan 4096 entries, 32 runs, 6 hours age, 64 latched records) and, when MV_HANDOFF_PATHS is unset, watches the newest private run directories; records older than the process need a matching human binding and a running srf-id/srf-pg container witnessed by docker with a 1000 ms timeout.

privateDirectory walks every path component with O_NOFOLLOW directory descriptors and requires the final directory to be owned by the user with mode 0700, else PRIVATE_PATH; private files must be 0600, user-owned and at most 65536 bytes (PRIVATE_FILE).
resolveIdentityTool prefers the bundled tool path and falls back to <MV_OPERATOR_REPO>/tools/mv_identity.py when MV_OPERATOR_REPO is an absolute normalised path and the bundled file is absent.

ui/electron/preload.js is the sandbox-loadable preload: it exposes one frozen facade as window.metaviewer that shapes every call (exact arity, string types, UTF-8 byte caps, closed channel set) before ipcRenderer.invoke; main re-validates every field, so preload never authorizes.

createPreloadFacade exposes the facade once under FACADE_NAME 'metaviewer' through contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld; load/save are enumerable, and the domain groups (capture, slots, settings, rewind, guestCommand, headless, authority, input, operator, frames, sideTerminal, clipboard, qa) are own immutable properties.
Preload throws ContractError with local codes DEPS, CHANNEL, ARGS, PAYLOAD and OUTCOME; message format is '<CODE>: <detail>', distinct from core refusal reasons.

assertFixedCall refuses CHANNEL ('channel outside the fixed preload set'), ARGS ('load takes no arguments' / 'save takes exactly one argument') and PAYLOAD when the save text is not a string or exceeds 256 KiB of UTF-8.

WIRE_NAMES maps facade methods to channels metaviewer:<suffix>, including settings.load/save, recording.destination, nested.depth, nested.self, authority.vmAvailable/propose/intent/createSurface/subscribe/unsubscribe, side-terminal.open/enabled/attach/resize/close/providers/copy, clipboard.writeText/readText, capsule-state.request, rewind.*, guest-command.* and headless.*.

wireCall throws CHANNEL ('unknown domain channel') for a channel outside the map and ARGS ('wrong arity') for the wrong argument count, except authority.createSurface which also accepts exactly {kind:'vm'}; payloads over 256 KiB fail PAYLOAD 'byte cap'.

Terminal calls are shape-checked: open needs command plus cols 2..500 and rows 2..300 (PAYLOAD 'terminal spec'); attach/close/resize refuse TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED for a malformed spec and TERMINAL_UNKNOWN_SESSION for a session id outside ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$.
Clipboard writes and terminal copy refuse ERR_CLIPBOARD_INVALID for missing, NUL-containing or oversize text; terminal copy text must be 1..128 chars of a capture id.

In a nested display-only window, capsule-state, terminal and clipboard calls throw DISPLAY_ONLY ('side-terminal is disabled in nested display'); a terminal session opened by another facade instance is refused TERMINAL_IO_REFUSED 'SENDER'.

authority.propose replies must be action_verdict/v0.2 with proposal_id, core_seq >= 1 and decision admitted or refused; a refused reason_code must be STALE_FRAME, SURFACE_NOT_AGENT_CONTROLLED, LOCKED_BY_OTHER, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, OUT_OF_BOUNDS or POLICY, else OUTCOME 'verdict'.
authority.createSurface returns exactly {ok:true} or {ok:false, code} with an upper-case code; any other reply throws OUTCOME 'create surface'.

The preload subscribes only to closed host push channels: metaviewer:authority.frames, capture.state, side-terminal.port, handoff.state, demo.state, headless.state, guest-command.state, guest-command.observation and rewind.state; any other channel throws CHANNEL 'subscription refused'.

installPreload's invoke refuses side-terminal and clipboard channels in nested mode (DISPLAY_ONLY), the QA anchor and frame-diagnostic channels unless enabled ('qa channel disabled', 'frame diag channel disabled'), and routes operator channels through assertOperatorCall.

The guarded CommonJS entry installs the facade with the real contextBridge and ipcRenderer and, except in nested mode, invokes metaviewer:renderer-ready once on window load as the third readiness witness.

Operator calls throw NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY in nested mode, OPERATOR_ARGS or OPERATOR_PAYLOAD for bad shapes (identity id ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$, label up to 128 chars without shell metacharacters, up to 16 sorted domains), and OPERATOR_REPLY when a reply is outside the closed set.
OPERATOR_METHODS is the closed operator vocabulary: entry.copy, demo.start/stop/prompt/check/state, identity.list/show/create/delete/login, egress.get/set and handoff.list/ack.

Accepted operator refusal codes are IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, IDENTITY_REFUSED, IDENTITY_PROTECTED, IDENTITY_BOUND, PROFILE_NOT_PROVISIONED, PROFILE_MISSING, NET_EGRESS_IO, NET_EGRESS_INVALID, NET_PROXIED_UNSUPPORTED, NET_OPEN_PREREQ and HANDOFF_UNAVAILABLE.

stateRequest throws CAPSULE_STATE_REQUEST unless the capsule-state request is capsule_state_request/v0.2 with op save/overwrite/load/copy/list/delete, slot and profile ids matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$ and a boolean credential_copy_confirmed; hostBindings imports this same check.

Surface input refusals are the closed set NOT_IN_CONTROL, SURFACE_UNKNOWN, STALE_STREAM, LIMIT, NESTED_DISPLAY_ONLY, SCHEMA and CORE_UNAVAILABLE; batches are capped at 32 events, 16 KiB, 1024 text chars, 256 queued events and 64 surfaces, with 20 ms type coalescing.

Validated frame notices with byte-plane ports are forwarded to the renderer main world by window.postMessage as {type:'metaviewer:frame-port', schema:'frame_port/v1'} with one transferred port, only when the origin is app://metaviewer; invalid notices close their ports.

ui/src/main.js is the renderer entry: it reads window.metaviewer once, builds layout storage, settings, authority runtime, terminal broker, capture and input ports (or fixture doubles for ?state= previews), then mounts App.vue on #metaviewer-app.

A missing preload facade throws 'Layout service unavailable'; refuseBoot then replaces the mount with the closed text 'MetaViewer cannot start: The application is unavailable. Please try again.' (or 'This preview is unavailable.' for preview query errors) and sets data-error-code (ERR_STARTUP_UNAVAILABLE unless the error is an ERR_* code).

Layout reads retry up to 100 times every 20 ms only while the invoke error says 'No handler registered' (main has not yet bound the handler); any other error marks load failed, and later saves throw LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED.
Settings are read once before the initial paint with the same retry rule; a failed read keeps defaults (scheme mv-dark, density compact) and the settings panel later gets ERR_SETTINGS_HOST.
The live frame-port router is imported lazily; if the import or install fails the router is null and tiles stay Connecting instead of refusing boot.
teardown disposes QA reporter, rehash reporter, frame router, capture state, input port and authority runtime on pagehide or app unmount.

ui/src/App.vue is the root shell view: navigation rail with the capsule tree, top bar with tile presets, the DesktopWorkspace wall, multislot, recording, settings, terminal dock, identities, catalog launcher and demo dialogs, all driven by props from ui/src/main.js.

buildWorkingTree is a pure function that turns admitted projection rows plus the desktop state into two views (Humans, Agents), each with desktops and capsules carrying title, kind (microvm, program, browser, unknown), status, tone, symbol and a notIsolated flag; it never treats ownership as activity.

Tree status precedence is: MicroVM phase, 'Needs you' (pending handoff), 'Lost', 'Recording automation', 'Error', 'Connecting', 'Minimized', 'Acting' (agent view only), then 'Human' or 'Agent'; symbols are record, triangle, warning for host windows, empty circle for lost, half circle for connecting.
navigationTree recomputes from rows plus MicroVM workload tiles, the desktop state, treeHandoffs, closed panels (shown as Minimized), program/app/browser metadata and the demo recording snapshot.

Tree handoff flags come from HandoffNotice: its pending event replaces treeHandoffs with surface ids that need the operator, which makes those capsules show 'Needs you' and the view heading show a dot.

refreshTreeMetadata reads listApps, programs and choices from window.metaviewerRoles (a separate preload, ui/electron/rolePreload.cjs) and keeps only icons that are base64 PNG/SVG data URLs and at most 256 apps; it reruns when the row set changes or the launcher closes, and stale generations are dropped.

Tree rename (double-click or F2 on a desktop or capsule) calls the wall's renameDesktop or renameCapsule; a false result or exception shows 'Name could not be saved.' as an alert under the view, and Enter saves while Escape cancels and restores focus.
Collapse state is a local map keyed '<view>/<desktop>' (not persisted); selecting a desktop switches the global view, selects it on the wall and expands it.

selectTreeCapsule ignores unknown ids or ids without a desktop assignment, otherwise selects the home desktop and reveals the capsule as a tab (or reveals the MicroVM workload) and marks the panel open.

The Remove empty desktop button is shown only when the active desktop is not desktop 1 and is disabled while any capsule is assigned to it; the Add desktop button is disabled until the desktop state loads or at MAX_DESKTOPS_PER_VIEW.

If layout read fails, workspaceStorage returns the default layout and the rail shows 'Layout unavailable. The default layout is shown read-only. Changes will not be saved.'; after a refused save it shows 'Changes cannot be saved in this session.' (LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED).

submitHost turns host refusals into a toast '<CODE>: <text>', for example RAM_ADMISSION_REFUSED 'Not enough free host memory to start another capsule (one capsule needs 6 GiB: 4 GiB RAM + 2 GiB shm)...', SURFACE_CREATE_BUSY, SURFACE_CREATE_TIMEOUT and SURFACE_CREATE_FAILED with install guidance; unknown codes get 'This request is unavailable. Please try again.'

onCreateCapsule refuses in the renderer before any host call: DISPLAY_ONLY in nested walls, PROGRAM_PROFILE_FORBIDDEN / WINDOW_PROFILE_FORBIDDEN when the renderer tries to pick a profile, PROGRAM_BINARY_REQUIRED, CAPSULE_ROLE_INVALID, WINDOW_CHOICE_REQUIRED, VM_SELECTOR_INVALID, VM_UNAVAILABLE and NO_BROWSER_CAPSULE.

createProgramCapsule returns HOST_PROGRAM_UNAVAILABLE ('program launching is not available on this host') when window.metaviewerRoles.createProgram is absent; createWindowCapsule returns HOST_WINDOW_UNAVAILABLE likewise.

Outside fixtures and nested mode, App polls window.metaviewerRoles.surfaces() every 250 ms and merges role surfaces (host windows marked notIsolated) into the projection feed; a SURFACE_AUTHORITY_MISMATCH item shows 'Capsule <id> is unavailable because its host state changed. Refresh Identities to check its state; other capsules remain available.'
The status bar text is 'Core connected' when the feed has an envelope, 'MicroVM ready · No frames needed', 'Waiting for capsule frames' when a runtime exists, else 'Core not connected'.

Settings, multislot, creative and terminal views are mutually exclusive: toggleSettings closes creative, multislot and terminal before flipping settings, and toggleTerminal does the same through a generation counter that drops stale opens.
VM availability is rechecked through authorityHost.vmAvailable every time the catalog launcher opens; a missing or failed answer keeps VM hidden.
rows admits projection rows that are not destroyed, not stopped locally, and lost only on live boots or diagnostic fixtures; in nested display-only mode they also pass applyNestedWall.
When an admitted id departs, App disarms its input, bumps its lifetime epoch, forgets reveal and closed-panel state and sends a close presentation intent to the wall.

App renders DesktopWorkspace with the merged feed, desktop state events, capture state, intent builders and tile scheduler; layout-error sets LAYOUT_SAVE_REFUSED and each surface slot renders RoleSurface plus SurfaceCanvas.

Wall refresh maps DESKTOP_CHANGED, PROJECTION_UNAVAILABLE, SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE and ERR_NOT_READY to user text such as 'Live capsule state is unavailable. Reconnect, then refresh.'; other failures show 'Wall refresh did not complete. Try again.'
